It then schedules pre-agreed advisor check-ins at day 3, 14, 45 and 90. The advisor gets a dashboard of which couples have done the drill and where their exposure is.
ideas.why_now: Cerulli's Sept 2026 work frames retention of the transfer as the priority, and 89% of surveyed firms call family meetings essential. Wealth managers are buying heir-engagement tools, yet the first wave of money is spousal and the widow is under-served. Cheap document ingestion and secure vaults make the kit affordable for small firms.
ideas.revenue_model: $300-$700 per household per year billed to the firm, or a $25-40K/yr platform fee for a 100-household book. The ROI pitch: keeping one $1.5M widow at a 1% fee is worth $15K a year.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The heir-retention narrative aims at the wrong person on the wrong day. Widows rarely leave over portfolio returns. They leave because nobody made the first 90 days easy. A rehearsal also works where estate planning fails, because people avoid 'planning' but will attend a scheduled drill.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit 3-5 RIAs through advisor communities and podcasts. Run drills by hand with a spreadsheet and printed binder for each firm's 10 oldest couples. Record time-to-locate-accounts and the number of single-point-of-failure findings. Charge a $2.5K pilot fee and turn the findings into a retention case study the advisor can show prospects.

ideas.title: Ceremony-as-a-Service for Direct Cremation Providers
ideas.one_liner: White-label the memorial gathering that low-cost cremation providers can't deliver, so families buy a $1.5K box of ashes plus a $3.5K send-off.
ideas.customer: Direct-cremation companies (online and storefront), hospices and community organizations. Families pay for the events.
ideas.problem: NFDA projects cremation at 63.4% in 2025, rising to 82.3% by 2045. Direct-cremation providers win on price but hand families ashes with no ceremony. Consolidators' chapels and $8K packages don't fit that customer. NFDA reports 58.3% of consumers have attended services at unconventional venues, so demand exists but no one owns the coordination.
ideas.solution: A 'Celebration Desk' embedded in the provider's checkout as 'add a gathering'. A coordinator plus software books non-funeral venues (breweries, restaurants, parks, boats, halls), catering, a celebrant, a slideshow, live-stream and RSVPs. Packages are fixed-price at $1,500, $3,500 or $7,500. It also handles scattering permits and follow-up.
ideas.why_now: Direct cremation share keeps climbing. NFDA says 61.4% of consumers are interested in green options. Consolidators are structurally pinned to a 58% cremation mix and 3%+ annual price increases and cannot copy an unbundled model. Venues have empty weekday capacity and live-streaming is now trivial.
ideas.revenue_model: Fixed package fee at 35-45% gross margin, 10-15% rev share from venues and caterers, and a referral or white-label fee of $150-$300 per booked event to the cremation provider.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Insiders see direct cremation as the industry's price-war threat. It is really an unbundling that turned the ceremony into a separate, high-margin purchase that nobody owns. The providers who created it have no event staff, and the consolidators' chapels are the wrong shape.
ideas.first_30_days: Pick one metro. Sign one direct-cremation provider and ten venues. Coordinate the first five events by hand at about $1,800 each, offered through the provider's post-arrangement email. Photograph and price each event to build the package catalog.

ideas.title: Post-Divorce Beneficiary Cleanup for Family Lawyers
ideas.one_liner: Sell divorce attorneys a flat-fee sweep that finds and fixes stale beneficiary designations, since the will is the least important estate document.
ideas.customer: Family-law attorneys and divorce mediators or CDFAs. The initial buyer is the law firm, which adds it to the closing checklist. It expands later to advisors and benefits platforms.
ideas.problem: Most middle-class wealth passes by beneficiary designation (401(k)s, IRAs, life insurance, TOD/POD accounts), not by will. For ERISA plans the plan documents generally control even when the divorce decree says otherwise (Egelhoff v. Egelhoff, Kennedy v. Plan Administrator). Clients rarely update every form. Ex-spouses get paid, second families litigate, and the lawyer faces malpractice exposure.
ideas.solution: A 'Post-Decree Beneficiary Sweep'. The client links accounts or uploads statements. Software plus a paralegal gets each custodian's current designation, compares it to the decree, will and trust, and produces a discrepancy report. It prepares custodian-specific change forms for e-signature and tracks each until confirmed. A yearly re-audit subscription follows, triggered by life events (birth, remarriage, death).
ideas.why_now: Account aggregation and LLM extraction from messy statements and custodian PDFs now make cross-custodian paperwork cheap. Retirement balances sit at record levels, and divorce among the over-50s ('grey divorce') has risen for decades. The transfer wave is putting designation errors in the spotlight.
ideas.revenue_model: $295-$495 flat per divorce billed as a firm disbursement, $79/yr monitoring, and an enterprise license to benefits platforms and advisors at roughly $1-3 per participant per year.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Everyone in estate planning talks about wills and trusts. The biggest mis-transfers happen through forms nobody re-reads. Divorce is the one moment when a lawyer, a deadline and malpractice fear are all in the room, so it is the cheapest place to sell an audit.
ideas.first_30_days: Sell to 10 solo and small family-law firms as a flat add-on. Process the first 20 cases manually with a paralegal and spreadsheet. Track the share of clients whose ex-spouse is still named anywhere (a hypothesis to measure) and turn that into a case study and a malpractice-avoidance pitch.

ideas.title: Heir-to-Own: Sibling Buyouts on Inherited Homes
ideas.one_liner: Help the sibling who wants to keep the family house buy out the others by assuming the parent's low-rate mortgage and financing the rest.
ideas.customer: Adult heirs inheriting a home worth $300K-$1.5M where at least one wants to keep it. Distribution runs through probate attorneys and mediators. Capital comes from credit unions and community lenders.
ideas.problem: The default assumption is that inherited homes get sold and split. The recurring fight is one heir wanting to keep the house while the others want cash. The keeper often can't qualify for a cash-out refinance, because the estate isn't closed, income is thin, or no cash is on hand, so the outcome is a forced sale, a partition suit or a family break.
ideas.solution: A platform that (1) gets a neutral valuation (AVM plus appraiser) and a transparent buyout formula, (2) generates a sibling agreement covering the buyout, occupancy and carrying costs, with attorney review, and (3) structures financing: assume or continue the parent's existing low-rate first mortgage, plus a second lien or HELOC from a partner lender, closing when the estate can convey. Start as a licensed mortgage broker packaging these deals.
ideas.why_now: A large share of US mortgages carry rates near 3-4%, so the parent's loan is now valuable. Federal rules (Garn-St Germain and the CFPB successor-in-interest rules) generally let heirs keep servicing on an inherited mortgage without triggering due-on-sale. Gen X stands to inherit about $14T in the next decade (Cerulli), and market rates make cash-out refinancing unattractive.
ideas.revenue_model: Origination or broker fees of 1-1.5%, a $500-$1,500 platform fee for valuation and agreement docs, and referral or spread income from the second-lien partner.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Locked-in low-rate mortgages turned the inherited house from an asset to liquidate into cheap capital to keep. The estate industry still defaults to 'sell', and lenders have no way to underwrite an heir with equity but no cash.
ideas.first_30_days: Pick one state. Sign five probate attorneys and one credit union. Get an MLO license or a broker partner. Handle three cases manually. Publish a free sibling-buyout calculator for estate forums and Facebook groups as the lead magnet.

ideas.title: Heirloom Fair-Division Engine for Sibling Estates
ideas.one_liner: Use a fair-division algorithm and a phone walkthrough to split a dead parent's belongings so nobody feels cheated.
ideas.customer: Executors (often the eldest child), estate attorneys, mediators and professional fiduciaries. Families pay $149-$399 per estate, or attorneys pay $99/month.
ideas.problem: Research on inheritance conflict (for example the University of Minnesota's 'Who Gets Grandma's Yellow Pie Plate?' work) finds sentimental personal property, not money, triggers most sibling fights. Executors improvise with turn-taking or a spreadsheet, distant siblings get shortchanged, and the house can't be sold until it is cleared.
ideas.solution: A phone walkthrough captures the house room by room, AI tags items, and each remote heir gets a private points budget to express wants. A fair-division algorithm (adjusted-winner or envy-free-up-to-one-item style) proposes an allocation with cash or point equalization. The app then coordinates shipping and pickup, and routes leftovers to donation with receipts or to sale. It ends with a signed distribution memo the attorney can file. Each item keeps a story card so its history survives.
ideas.why_now: Multimodal AI can inventory objects from video, and phone-based 3D capture is mainstream. Boomer households hold decades of belongings that Millennial and Gen X heirs scattered across the country often don't want. With the federal estate tax largely out of the picture for most families (reported $15M exemption), family conflict is the main remaining risk.
ideas.revenue_model: Per-estate fee ($149-$399), 10-15% margin on shipping and donation logistics, and attorney seats at $99/month.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The fights are about objects, not dollars. Objects are one of the few asset classes with a known mechanism-design solution, and no estate product uses it.
ideas.first_30_days: Build a no-code prototype with a spreadsheet points auction. Offer it free to 20 executors found in estate-help forums and groups. Ask elder-law attorneys to use it as a mediation-lite deliverable and convert 5 of them to paid. Time-box the whole thing to about three weeks per estate.

ideas.title: Aid-in-Dying Program-in-a-Box for Hospices
ideas.one_liner: Sell newly-legal states' hospices and health systems the policies, forms, trained consulting-clinician panel and logistics they need to participate in medical aid in dying.
ideas.customer: Independent hospices, palliative practices and non-religious health systems in Illinois and New York, then Massachusetts and Pennsylvania if they pass. The buyer is the medical director or administrator.
ideas.problem: Legalization creates a right on paper. The bottleneck is willing, trained clinicians (attending plus consulting physician, and mental-health evaluation where required), statutory documentation, waiting periods, pharmacy sourcing and staff opt-out policies. Most providers have no playbook, so patients bounce between systems that opt out. Advocacy groups cover navigation, not staffing.
ideas.solution: A turnkey program: policy templates, staff training, state-specific e-documentation workflows, an on-call roster of trained consulting physicians and evaluators (licensed per state, telehealth where allowed), pharmacy coordination, family support, and post-death reporting. The service serves only patient-initiated requests and supports providers that opt in.
ideas.why_now: New York's law was signed Feb 6, 2026, and Illinois's law, signed Dec 12, 2025, takes effect this month (Sept 2026). Two large states are opening within months, with 14 jurisdictions now having some form of law and more pending. Scheduled deaths also create planning lead time that sudden deaths never had.
ideas.revenue_model: $15-40K program onboarding fee, $500-$1,000 per consult or evaluation, and per-case coordination fees. State grants are possible.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The scarce input is not legal permission but willing clinicians and paperwork bandwidth, so the money is in clinical capacity and compliance, which advocacy nonprofits don't provide.
ideas.first_30_days: Sign 2-3 physicians with prior Oregon or Washington experience as advisors. Approach 10 independent Illinois hospices. Sell a $7.5K readiness assessment plus policy pack first. Start recruiting a consulting-physician roster and get counsel to confirm state rules on telehealth and referral fees.

ideas.title: Executor-of-Last-Resort for Solo Agers
ideas.one_liner: A subscription that names a licensed fiduciary as your executor and runs daily wellness checks, so a childless retiree isn't found weeks late and handed to a court-appointed stranger.
ideas.customer: Unpartnered or childless adults 65+ with $100K-$1.5M estates (too small for most corporate trustees, too large to ignore), plus their elder-law attorneys, senior living communities and Area Agencies on Aging.
ideas.problem: Solo agers have no obvious executor, agent or emergency contact, and named friends or nieces often flake. Japan shows the downstream effect: 37,227 people living alone were found dead at home in H1 2024, nearly 4,000 undiscovered for over a month. The US has no equivalent service layer, and intestate estates go to public administrators.
ideas.solution: A 'Stewardship Plan'. (a) A licensed professional fiduciary or trust company partner agrees to serve as successor agent and executor. (b) Passive wellness signals (phone, smart speaker, utility use, optional wearable) plus a daily automated or human check-in escalate to neighbors and welfare checks. (c) A digital go-bag holds accounts, medications, pets, keys and funeral wishes. (d) At death it triggers funeral instructions, securing the house, clear-out and estate administration for a fee schedule.
ideas.why_now: Cheap ambient signals and voice-AI check-in calls make monitoring inexpensive. Death care is proving roll-up-able (Everstory, SCI), yet no one serves the years before death for people without heirs. Estates and consolidator data show volume is flat, so services attached to existing customers are where growth sits.
ideas.revenue_model: $39-$79/month subscription, executor fees at death (often statutory, a few percent of the estate), margin on clear-out and estate services, and B2B fees from senior living and AAAs.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The first customer isn't dying. She is buying certainty that someone competent shows up on the worst day. Subscriptions fund the acquisition of a low-cost executor book that pays out later.
ideas.first_30_days: Partner with a licensed fiduciary in one state. Sign 3 elder-law attorneys. Recruit a 30-person waitlist through senior centers and 'elder orphan' groups. Charge $99 setup plus $49/month and run the daily check-in calls manually at first.

ideas.title: Posthumous Likeness Trusts for Creators
ideas.one_liner: Estate planning for people whose face and voice already earn money: who may license their AI replica, who may not, and how it is enforced.
ideas.customer: Mid-tier creators (100K-5M followers), podcasters, voice actors, and the small managers and MCNs who represent them.
ideas.problem: Consumer-grade video and voice cloning means anyone's likeness can be recreated after death. Laws are a patchwork (Tennessee's ELVIS Act and California's 2024 digital-replica laws, a federal NO FAKES bill pending). Creators' estates hold real income (channels, catalogs, sponsorships) but have no instrument to permit, forbid or license replicas. Platforms handle it ad hoc.
ideas.solution: A 'Likeness Trust Kit': (1) a will or trust addendum with a digital-replica directive (allowed uses, revenue splits, ban list, who decides), (2) a registry and notice system aimed at platforms and AI vendors, (3) monitoring for unauthorized replicas and template takedowns, (4) a channel-continuity plan (access, memorialization, pinned messages), and (5) an optional licensing desk for approved 'legacy' uses.
ideas.why_now: The fall-2025 backlash over AI videos of deceased public figures made estates' concerns public. State post-mortem publicity laws changed in 2024, and platforms have begun shipping likeness-detection tools for creators (verify current status). No estate product has priced in that a voice and face are now licensable and misusable assets.
ideas.revenue_model: $1,500-$3,500 setup for documents and registry, $19-$79/month monitoring, and 10-20% of licensed uses. Managers buy in bulk.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Estate lawyers treat likeness as a celebrity issue. The willing buyers are working creators who already understand platforms and already earn from their persona, and they are numerous and reachable through managers.
ideas.first_30_days: Partner with an entertainment attorney. Draft a template addendum. Sell to 10 creator managers at about $2K per client. Use off-the-shelf detection tools for monitoring and publish a public 'creator death checklist' for lead generation.

ideas.title: Contest-Proof Signing: Capacity Sessions for Wills
ideas.one_liner: A recorded, clinician-run capacity and intent session at will signing, so a later contest by disappointed heirs has strong evidence against it.
ideas.customer: Estate-planning and elder-law attorneys and RIAs whose clients are 75+, in blended families or making unequal bequests. Clients pay the clinical entity directly, and firms bundle it into fixed-fee packages.
ideas.problem: An older wealthy cohort, more second marriages and rising dementia diagnoses mean more disputes about capacity and undue influence. Evidence of capacity at signing is usually the drafting lawyer's memory plus boilerplate. That is weak in court and expensive to defend.
ideas.solution: A standardized signing-day product. A licensed geriatric psychiatrist or neuropsychologist runs a structured, recorded interview with validated screening, an independent private conversation without family, and a recorded 'why I chose this' statement. The bundle is hashed and stored under the attorney's privilege, with an optional yearly refresh and in-home or remote delivery.
ideas.why_now: FDA cleared blood tests for Alzheimer's pathology in 2025, so more people get an early diagnosis and want to sign while they still can. Remote notarization and e-will laws widened access, and video is cheap. The transfer is concentrated in older households with complex families.
ideas.revenue_model: $700-$1,500 per session billed by the clinical entity, firm-level packages of $25K/year, and yearly refresh sessions. Lawyer referral-fee rules make direct client billing the safer structure (check state ethics rules).
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Capacity is a moment-in-time question and the evidence is manufactured at the signing. It is cheap to create then and impossible to recreate later. Diagnosis awareness is creating a rush window nobody is serving.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit 3 geriatric psychiatrists or neuropsychologists per metro. Partner with 5 elder-law firms. Run 20 sessions at $900 and have each firm's litigators review the artifact bundle. Keep clean records of what each session found.

ideas.title: ILIT Rescue After the Estate-Tax Cliff Disappeared
ideas.one_liner: A paid, documented review of irrevocable life insurance trusts built to pay estate tax that most families will never owe.
ideas.customer: Trustees (individuals and bank or trust companies), estate attorneys, and families holding ILITs with policies of $1M-$25M.
ideas.problem: For decades planners sold ILITs to fund federal estate tax. With the reported $15M-per-person exemption from 2026 (verify), many of these families will never owe it. Trusts keep paying premiums on policies that may be unnecessary, underfunded or poorly performing. Trustees fear fiduciary liability for doing nothing, yet nobody is paid to run the review.
ideas.solution: A 'trust-policy triage' service. Ingest the trust document and in-force illustration, classify the trust's purpose, and produce a decision memo: keep, reduce, 1035-exchange, sell, decant or terminate. It documents a prudent-process file for the trustee. Then execute through licensed partners (settlement broker, insurance agency, trust counsel).
ideas.why_now: The 2025 tax law reportedly raised and indexed the exclusion. About 10M life policies lapse per year (per the brief's cited market data), and the life-settlement market has active buyers (Coventry, Abacus). Wealth flows to heirs are large enough that leaving policy value on the table is now visible.
ideas.revenue_model: $2,500-$7,500 review fee per trust plus success fees on settled or exchanged policies where licensing allows.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Fiduciary duty turns optimization into a mandatory review: trustees are exposed if they do nothing, so someone must be paid to produce the file even when the answer is 'keep'.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit 2 estate attorneys and a licensed life-settlement broker. Pitch corporate trustees' special-assets desks. Run 10 reviews at a $1,500 intro price and learn which outcomes come up most.

ideas.title: Court-Ready Estate Accounting from Bank Statements
ideas.one_liner: Upload the statements and get the court's accounting format back, so small probate firms stop losing money on the ledger.
ideas.customer: Solo and small estate and trust law firms, CPAs acting as fiduciaries, professional fiduciaries, and small trust desks at community banks.
ideas.problem: Inventories, receipts-and-disbursements accountings and trust accountings to beneficiaries take 10-30+ hours per estate. Each state and county wants a different format. Small firms bill flat fees or lose money, and errors cause objections and surcharges.
ideas.solution: Upload bank and brokerage statements (PDF or CSV). The system categorizes transactions into principal and income, ties to date-of-death balances, flags unusual disbursements, and exports state-format accountings. Start with California plus one more high-volume state (New York or Pennsylvania). A reviewer trail records every override. Later add fiduciary 1041 data and distribution schedules.
ideas.why_now: LLM document extraction only recently became reliable on messy statements. Revocable-trust use has grown with online will and trust providers, so more successor trustees face accounting duties.
ideas.revenue_model: $149-$399 per accounting or $199-$499/month per firm, with enterprise pricing for banks.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck in probate isn't drafting, it's the ledger, and the ledger is what judges and beneficiaries inspect. Whoever owns the estate ledger owns the workflow and the data for tax, inventory and distributions.
ideas.first_30_days: Pick California. Recruit 10 small firms through bar section lists. Process 20 accountings manually for $199 each while capturing the county format rules. Publish a sample output for lead generation.

ideas.title: Step-Up Basis Files for Inherited Assets
ideas.one_liner: Sell CPAs and estate lawyers a cheap, defensible date-of-death valuation packet for every inherited house or portfolio.
ideas.customer: CPAs and enrolled agents preparing 1040s and 1041s for heirs, estate attorneys, and heirs selling inherited homes or securities.
ideas.problem: The step-up in basis (IRC 1014) is the biggest tax break most families receive, but only if the heir can support date-of-death value. Below the estate-tax threshold no appraisal is required, so heirs sell years later with no valuation and risk the IRS asserting the parent's low original cost. Securities and crypto also need clean date-of-death pricing.
ideas.solution: A $150-$400 per-asset packet: houses (AVM plus retrospective appraiser sign-off), securities (date-of-death pricing), crypto, collectibles. It outputs a Basis Memo for the CPA's file, stores it, and alerts the heir when the property lists for sale.
ideas.why_now: The higher federal exemption (reported $15M) means fewer estates file a Form 706 that would have documented values. Home prices are sharply higher than a few years ago, so embedded gains are large. Boomers are the source of most transfers.
ideas.revenue_model: Per-report fees, CPA firm subscriptions, and appraiser marketplace margin.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The tax benefit is lost through missing paperwork, not law. A small, cheap document created at death protects a large tax saving years later.
ideas.first_30_days: Sell to 15 CPA firms and 5 estate attorneys. Use an AVM API plus 3 contract appraisers per metro. Deliver in 5 business days and gather feedback on what the CPAs actually attach to returns.

ideas.title: Vacant Inherited-Home Insurance and Caretaking
ideas.one_liner: A bundled insurance-plus-sensors-plus-caretaker program for the house that sits empty during probate.
ideas.customer: Executors and heirs of a decedent's home, reached through probate attorneys, funeral homes and hospice social workers. Insurers and MGAs are the capacity partners.
ideas.problem: Homeowners policies typically restrict coverage for vandalism, freezing and other perils once a home is vacant 30-60 days, which is exactly when no probate court has appointed anyone. Probate often takes 9-18 months (unverified estimate). A burst pipe or break-in lands on an amateur executor, who may be personally exposed. Property taxes and utilities also keep running.
ideas.solution: An MGA-backed 'Estate Home Program' with a vacant-dwelling policy placed with a surplus-lines carrier, water and temperature sensors, weekly visits, lock rekeying and mail handling, utility transfer to the executor, and an optional executor advance for carrying costs repaid at sale. Add clean-out and sale-prep referrals.
ideas.why_now: Housing wealth is starting to flow from Boomers. Insurers tightened property underwriting after recent nonrenewal waves, and cheap IoT sensors make monitoring practical.
ideas.revenue_model: MGA commission (10-20%), a $150-$300/month program fee, and margin on clean-out and sale-prep referrals.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The house effectively becomes uninsurable at the exact moment the owner dies, and nobody owns that timing gap. Executors find out after the loss.
ideas.first_30_days: Find an E&S broker who writes vacant dwellings and design a 'vacant estate' placement. Sign 5 probate attorneys and test with 10 houses. Confirm state vacancy and insurable-interest rules with a licensed agent.

ideas.title: Overnight First-Call Co-op for Independent Funeral Homes
ideas.one_liner: A shared night-and-weekend answering, dispatch and chain-of-custody service so small funeral homes never lose a call at 2 a.m.
ideas.customer: Independent funeral homes, especially 1-3 director shops. NFDA counts 15,401 US funeral homes, about 75% family or privately owned. Hospice and hospital partners are the second audience.
ideas.problem: Small homes burn out staff on overnight first calls or miss them. Each service is worth several thousand dollars: SCI reports average revenue per service of $5,985. Hospitals want fast pickups, and chain-of-custody mistakes are catastrophic in an industry facing scrutiny after high-profile scandals.
ideas.solution: A shared first-call desk with trained answering, dispatch to a vetted licensed removal network, and a QR-tag custody app (ID verification, photos, timestamps) from bedside to the home's cooler. Add a hospital-facing release portal and overflow transfers later.
ideas.why_now: Consolidators keep gaining scale while independents face labor constraints. Volume is flat (SCI -1.4% in Q2 2026), so each lost call matters. Post-scandal regulatory attention raises the value of documented custody.
ideas.revenue_model: Per-dispatch fees ($175-$400 by distance), $199-$499/month retainers, and software add-ons.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Independents fear losing the call more than losing on price, and the call is decided in the first hour. Owning that hour makes you the switching layer between hospitals and independents.
ideas.first_30_days: Pick one metro. Recruit 10 independents and 3 removal contractors. Run the phone desk yourself and charge about $250 per call. Log every call to build a service-level report.

ideas.title: Repatriation-of-Remains Concierge for Immigrant Families
ideas.one_liner: A fixed-price service that gets a loved one's body home across borders, and later a low-cost membership that pre-funds it.
ideas.customer: Immigrant families on one corridor at a time (for example US to Mexico or Central America, the Philippines, India or Nigeria), plus consulates, churches, mosques, community associations and funeral homes without international skills.
ideas.problem: Sending remains home costs thousands (often $5-15K, unverified) and requires consular paperwork, health permits, embalming, sealed caskets, air cargo rules and destination-side logistics. Families use GoFundMe, church collections and opaque middlemen, in days, while grieving.
ideas.solution: Intake in the family's language, document assembly (consulate forms, permits), a vetted network of embalmers, cargo forwarders and destination funeral homes, insurance and payment plans, and one coordinator. Later add a $8-$15/month repatriation membership underwritten through a licensed insurer partner.
ideas.why_now: Community payment and remittance rails are digital, translation and document assembly are cheap with AI, and immigrant communities are large and trust-network driven. Funeral homes treat this as an add-on they don't understand.
ideas.revenue_model: 15-25% service margin on $6-12K cases, membership fees, and insurer commissions.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The mainstream industry treats repatriation as a sideline, but for these families it is the primary product. Corridor-specific know-how is the moat, and trust travels through churches and consulates.
ideas.first_30_days: Choose one corridor and one metro. Partner with a funeral home that already does it. Sign 3 churches or a consulate liaison. Run 5 cases at cost to document the exact process and price it.

ideas.title: Under-Canopy Grave Detection Survey Service
ideas.one_liner: Find unmarked graves before the bulldozer does, using drone LiDAR that sees through trees, machine-learning triage and targeted ground-penetrating radar.
ideas.customer: Municipalities, state DOTs, developers, title companies, utilities and solar or pipeline builders, plus churches and heritage nonprofits.
ideas.problem: Lost and unrecorded burial grounds are usually discovered when earthmovers hit them, causing delay, cost and heartbreak. Historic cemeteries, especially those of marginalized communities, are often undocumented. GPR surveys are slow, costly per acre and limited by scarce operators. There is no burial-risk layer in due diligence.
ideas.solution: Drone LiDAR and photogrammetry across large tracts to detect depressions and anomalies under canopy, ML-ranked into a probability map, followed by targeted GPR verification of the top candidates. Deliver a survey report and a registry entry. Add LLM reading of handwritten cemetery and church records.
ideas.why_now: Survey-grade drone LiDAR is now cheap, ML for GPR and terrain anomalies has matured, and rural land is being cleared quickly for solar, data centers and pipelines. LLMs can now read handwritten historic records. Everstory's drone mapping of about 400 cemeteries shows the method works for known sites.
ideas.revenue_model: $200-$1,500 per acre depending on terrain and depth, annual subscriptions for DOTs and utilities, and data licensing to title insurers.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Every earthmoving project carries burial-risk liability that appears in no database. The same survey serves developers, heritage groups and families, so it can be financed by the party with the most to lose.
ideas.first_30_days: Pilot with 2 churches or heritage groups on grant-funded work. Rent a LiDAR drone and pitch 5 solar developers on due-diligence add-ons. Recruit a GPR contractor and a cultural-resources archaeologist for sign-off.

ideas.title: Tell Us Once: US Death-Event Switchboard
ideas.one_liner: Verify an executor once, then let agents notify and close dozens of institutions for you, building toward a reusable 'authority to act' credential the institutions accept.
ideas.customer: Executors and surviving families pay, with distribution through funeral homes, estate attorneys and employers or insurers. Institutions later pay per verified case.
ideas.problem: US executors call dozens of banks, card issuers, utilities and subscription companies, each demanding its own certified death certificate, letters and forms. The deceased's identity is exposed to fraud. The UK has 'Tell Us Once', the US has nothing, and the brief finds no dominant software owner of the estate close-out workflow.
ideas.solution: The executor uploads the death certificate, ID and letters. The system verifies them once, then voice and browser agents run institution-specific playbooks: credit bureau alerts, identity locks, marketing suppression, subscription and utility cancellations or transfers, date-of-death balance requests and claim forms. A status board tracks every account, and human ops handle exceptions. Over time it issues a verified executor credential institutions accept by API.
ideas.why_now: Voice agents that navigate phone trees and hold queues, and browser agents that complete web forms, reached usable reliability in 2025-26. Digital ID wallets are spreading. Insurer and employer channels such as Empathy (50M+ covered policyholders) show buyers for bereavement services, but Empathy is not a close-out execution layer.
ideas.revenue_model: $199-$399 flat per estate ($99 wholesale to funeral homes), $10-$40 per verified case from institutions, and insurer or employer benefit contracts.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is repeated verification, not the work itself. A reusable, verified authority credential collapses 60 identical fights into one and gives institutions a fraud-reduction reason to cooperate.
ideas.first_30_days: Build playbooks for the top 30 institutions (big banks, card issuers, brokers, telecoms, streaming, credit bureaus). Sell 25 human-in-the-loop cases through 5 funeral homes at $149. Record each institution's requirements to build the data moat.

ideas.title: Courthouse-Handwriting Graph to Clear Heirs' Property
ideas.one_liner: Use AI that can read old handwritten deeds and probate files to map who really owns family land that never went through probate, and sell clean title to the buyers who need it.
ideas.customer: Solar, wind, pipeline and broadband developers, land trusts and conservation buyers, timber and ag buyers, and title insurers, with legal-aid partners protecting heirs.
ideas.problem: When a landowner dies without probate, title fragments among dozens of heirs. Developers can't lease or buy without consent, and heirs can lose land through partition sales. The records are handwritten across probate, deed and marriage files, so clearing one parcel takes lawyers weeks or months.
ideas.solution: LLM handwriting recognition over courthouse records builds a family-of-record graph per parcel, ranks probable heirs, finds them, and manages consent, lease or purchase packages through e-signature. Partner attorneys file quiet-title or partition actions for hard cases. Developers get a 'title-readiness score' per parcel. The design bakes in fair terms and legal aid for heirs.
ideas.why_now: Multimodal models now read historical cursive at near-human accuracy, and county records are increasingly scanned. The Uniform Partition of Heirs Property Act has been adopted in a couple dozen states, which pushes toward consensual deals. The land rush for solar and data-center sites needs clean title fast.
ideas.revenue_model: $2K-$10K per cleared parcel paid by the developer or a percentage of lease value, plus data licensing to title insurers.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The transfer that never went through probate, family land passed informally for generations, is a hidden inventory of blocked assets. Now a buyer with money (energy and data infrastructure) will pay to clear it.
ideas.first_30_days: Pick one county in a solar-active area with high heirs' property prevalence. Get a developer's list of blocked parcels. Process 10 parcels and partner with a heirs' property legal clinic to review the process and heir outreach.

ideas.title: Post-Mortem CT Plus Remote Pathology for Coroners
ideas.one_liner: Give rural coroners a scan-and-remote-read pathway so cause-of-death answers arrive in a day instead of weeks, without buying a single scanner.
ideas.customer: County coroners and medical examiners in rural or under-resourced jurisdictions, state ME systems, and hospitals with after-hours CT capacity.
ideas.problem: There is a well-documented shortage of forensic pathologists. Many rural coroners are elected non-physicians, autopsies are outsourced hundreds of miles away with multi-week backlogs, and each autopsy costs thousands. Families can't finalize burial or estates without a death certificate.
ideas.solution: A protocol in which the body is scanned on a hospital CT off-hours (or a mobile unit), with external-exam photos uploaded to a network of board-certified forensic pathologists and radiologists. AI triage flags fractures, hemorrhage and foreign objects, and the coroner gets a 24-hour read with a recommendation on whether a full autopsy is needed. The coroner keeps statutory authority.
ideas.why_now: Post-mortem CT is routine in several countries, imaging AI has matured, and telepathology infrastructure exists. The forensic pathology shortage persists, and overdose and heat deaths have strained offices.
ideas.revenue_model: $600-$1,200 per case plus $30-$60K/year county retainers, with rental fees to hospitals for scanner time.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The slowest step in death care isn't the funeral, it's the death certificate, and each day of delay costs families and insurers. A software-plus-network layer can loosen the choke point without owning capital equipment.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit 3-5 forensic pathologists (retired or part-time) as remote readers. Approach 5 backlogged rural coroners and one rural hospital about a pilot. Expect pilot signing within 6 months, with full revenue closer to 12.

ideas.title: AI-Native Estate Settlement Firm Under Arizona ABS
ideas.one_liner: A licensed alternative business structure that runs uncontested probate and small-estate work end-to-end at a flat fee, with attorneys supervising agent-driven workflows.
ideas.customer: Families of decedents in Arizona with $100K-$2M estates (uncontested probates, small-estate affidavits, simple trust administration), referred by funeral homes, hospices, senior living communities and advisors.
ideas.problem: Hourly or percentage probate fees don't work for $300K estates, so many attorneys decline them. Families face 9-18 months (unverified estimate) and $5-20K bills, run by an overwhelmed executor.
ideas.solution: An Arizona ABS-licensed law firm using agent workflows for documents, court filings, creditor notices, asset inventory, accountings and distributions, with attorney supervision at ratios far above traditional practice. Fixed price ($2,900-$6,500) with a timeline guarantee, payable from the estate at closing, and one point of contact. Add-ons include real estate sale and tax return preparation.
ideas.why_now: Arizona has permitted non-lawyer ownership of law firms since 2021 and Utah runs a sandbox. LLMs are now reliable enough for supervised legal drafting, and Arizona has a large retiree population. The brief's estimate of $5T of yearly transfers is heavily weighted to the very wealthy, leaving middle-class estates unserved.
ideas.revenue_model: Flat fees plus ancillary margin on property sales, tax preparation and accounting.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Hourly legal billing can't profitably serve middle-class estates, but a licensed software-first structure can undercut on price while earning better margins. The regulatory sandbox is both wedge and moat.
ideas.first_30_days: Apply for the ABS license or white-label under an existing ABS. Sign 3 funeral homes or senior communities for referrals. Run the first cases with a supervising attorney, and get counsel to review unauthorized-practice and fee-sharing rules.

ideas.title: Certified Refurb Phone Pipeline for Africa
ideas.one_liner: The memory crunch kills the cheap new phone, so the next wave of African users arrives on graded, warrantied used handsets.
ideas.customer: Independent phone retailers and mid-size distributors in Nigeria, Kenya and Ghana, and telco handset-financing programmes.
ideas.problem: Memory is 30-40% of a phone's bill of materials, IDC calls sub-Rs 9,000 phones possibly permanently uneconomical, and the GSMA $40 phone is only a pilot. About 960M Africans under coverage are still offline, and the used-phone market is full of blacklisted, dying-battery lemons.
ideas.solution: Buy bulk trade-in lots from the Gulf, EU and Japan and grade them in software (battery health, IMEI/blacklist check, Play certification). Ship with a 6-month warranty and sell to retailers on 30-day credit. The wedge is IMEI-clean, warrantied lots for a handful of retailers in one market such as Lagos.
ideas.why_now: 2026 AI-driven memory prices broke the sub-$60 new-phone tier, and LatAm shipments fell 10%. The GSMA is piloting a $40 phone precisely because the market cannot produce one.
ideas.revenue_model: Roughly $8-15 gross margin per handset, plus warranty fees and a financing spread.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Insiders wait for cheap new phones. The scarce asset is trust in used devices, and whoever certifies them owns the affordable tier once new supply disappears.
ideas.first_30_days: Source about 500 units from a Dubai or European refurbisher, grade them and place them with five retailers on consignment. Track return rates, which become the pricing moat.

ideas.title: Multi-Rail Cash-Flow Underwriting After UPI Fees
ideas.one_liner: When UPI stops being free for big tickets, reconstruct small-merchant revenue from GST, bank and supplier data instead of UPI alone.
ideas.customer: NBFCs, small finance banks and cash-flow lenders that lend to kirana and small retail businesses.
ideas.problem: Lenders assumed UPI data was the universal truth for underwriting. The Oct 15 MDR (0.4% above Rs 2,000, capped at Rs 300) hits about 4% of P2M volume but about 66% of value, so merchants now have a reason to route big tickets through cash or bank transfer.
ideas.solution: An API that combines Account Aggregator bank data, GST e-invoice and filing data, supplier invoices and soundbox/QR data into a revenue estimate with a rail-shift adjustment. The wedge is a turnover sanity-check score for five NBFCs.
ideas.why_now: MDR starts Oct 15, the Supreme Court refused a stay, and retailers are organising protests. RBI's cash-flow lending push depends on this data.
ideas.revenue_model: Rs 40-120 per scored application plus a monitoring fee on the live loan book.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: A fee on exactly the high-value 66% creates an incentive to hide it. The rail shift is a data-quality shock, and the first lender to model it gets an underwriting edge.
ideas.first_30_days: Get consented data on about 200 existing borrowers from one NBFC partner and backtest against repayments. Offer a 60-day free pilot.

ideas.title: Stablecoin Cash-Out Float for Corner Shops
ideas.one_liner: Stablecoins made sending money nearly free, so the scarce thing is cash at the last mile, and the margin goes to whoever finances the agents.
ideas.customer: Pharmacies, tiendas and kiosks that act as cash-out agents in Colombia, Mexico, Argentina and Nigeria, plus the stablecoin remittance and wallet apps that need them.
ideas.problem: A $200 US-to-Colombia transfer costs $12.13 on legacy rails versus about $0.01 in stablecoins, but recipients still want local cash. Small agents run out of float and refuse large withdrawals.
ideas.solution: A float-management app that shows each agent's cash position, advances intraday float against next-day USDC settlement and routes recipients to agents with liquidity. The wedge is 100 pharmacies on one remittance corridor for a single anchor partner.
ideas.why_now: Nigeria opened a stablecoin sandbox (Aug 12) and Kenya passed digital-currency legislation (Aug 6). Yellow Card is hiring in LatAm and SEA, and Felix has processed $8B over WhatsApp.
ideas.revenue_model: A 1-1.5% spread on float turnover plus a per-payout fee from the remitter.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: As stablecoin transfer fees go to zero, the margin migrates to the last ten metres of physical cash. This is cash logistics dressed up as fintech.
ideas.first_30_days: Sign one wallet or remittance partner as anchor and raise a roughly $50k float line from a debt fund. Onboard 20 pharmacies in one city.

ideas.title: Licensed Local-Language Speech Data Exchange
ideas.one_liner: Pay radio stations and call centers for rights-cleared audio and resell it to the voice-AI builders who cannot get it anywhere else.
ideas.customer: Voice-AI startups and model labs that need low-resource African and Indian language audio; radio stations and telco call centers are the suppliers.
ideas.problem: Foreign APIs are unusable for local voice because of latency and jitter. Startups like AethexAI train small models on call-center recordings and radio audio, but rights, cleaning and transcription are ad hoc.
ideas.solution: A consented, speaker-anonymised and transcribed archive with clear licences and revenue share for stations. The wedge is 3-5 stations in one language (Hausa, Yoruba or Swahili), with a sample set for a paying pilot.
ideas.why_now: 300M-1.7B parameter voice models now work in production, and Intron covers 57 languages. Labs face scrutiny over scraped data, and Sarvam and AethexAI are raising money.
ideas.revenue_model: $20-80 per cleaned, licensed hour, with 40-50% shared with the station, plus annual subscriptions.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Insiders assume low-resource data is unsellable because the markets are poor. The buyers are well-funded labs, and rights-cleared audio, not raw audio, is the bottleneck.
ideas.first_30_days: Sign three stations, digitise about 2,000 hours and clean 200 as a sample. Sell a paid pilot dataset to one voice-AI startup.

ideas.title: Kitchen Circuit Retrofit for India's Induction Switch
ideas.one_liner: Induction demand is real but low-income wiring cannot handle it, so sell the safe electrical retrofit and finance it.
ideas.customer: Lower-income urban households and resident welfare associations, reached through local electricians and hardware shops; discoms and state schemes can co-fund.
ideas.problem: After the LPG shortage, induction cooktop demand jumped 20-25x, the government is handing out 500k stoves, and the shift could add up to 27 GW. The Hindu reports low-income uptake is sluggish because of old wiring, overloaded meters and no financing.
ideas.solution: A pre-certified plug-and-play kit: dedicated 16A circuit, MCB/RCCB, heavy-duty socket and load-limiting smart plug, installed in two hours and paid in 12 EMIs. The wedge is 500 homes in one city through about 30 electricians.
ideas.why_now: The Hormuz energy shock created panic demand in March 2026, and the grid and household wiring are the binding constraint.
ideas.revenue_model: Rs 2,500-4,000 per kit and install at about 30% margin, plus an EMI spread and programme fees from discoms.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Everyone counts stoves sold. The bottleneck is the last 15 metres of copper, and the first fire wave will turn certified retrofits into a regulated must-buy.
ideas.first_30_days: Design the kit with a licensed electrical engineer and pre-sell it through 20 electricians and one housing association.

ideas.title: Solar Defection Radar for African Utilities
ideas.one_liner: Africa's invisible solar and battery boom leaves utilities, banks and insurers blind, so measure it district by district.
ideas.customer: African distribution utilities and regulators, development finance institutions, commercial banks and insurers.
ideas.problem: Africa installs 17 GW in 2026 (+45%), 75% of it distributed. Ember's estimates are 2x official figures, and only 14 of 54 countries reported 2025 data. Utilities cannot see which paying customers are leaving, and lenders cannot price the assets.
ideas.solution: Estimate installed solar and battery stock per district from customs and import data, rooftop detection in satellite imagery and installer sales data. The wedge is a quarterly district-level report for Nigeria or Kenya, sold to one utility and one DFI.
ideas.why_now: Chinese exports hit records and batteries now outsell panels in import dollars. Ember's 'invisible boom' finding is public but nobody has productised it.
ideas.revenue_model: $25-100k per year per institution, plus bespoke studies for DFIs.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: When self-generation outruns official statistics, the first credible dataset becomes the reference for tariffs, credit and insurance pricing.
ideas.first_30_days: Combine public Chinese export data, Ember figures and roof imagery for Lagos and Kano. Give a free sample to three utilities and one DFI.

ideas.title: Corridor-Pivot Recruiting for Displaced Gulf Migrants
ideas.one_liner: When Gulf jobs disappear, retrain returnees and place them in Japan, Taiwan and Germany with the employer paying the fee.
ideas.customer: Employers in care, construction and manufacturing in East Asia and Europe that pay placement fees; the workers pay nothing.
ideas.problem: About $50bn of Gulf remittances is at risk. Returnees in Kerala, Nepal, Bangladesh and the Philippines carry recruitment debts and Gulf-specific credentials, and predatory agents will push them into worse corridors.
ideas.solution: A skills-credential wallet, language bootcamp and employer-paid placement pipeline, operated through a licensed recruitment partner. The wedge is care workers and welders from Kerala and Nepal for one Japanese or German employer.
ideas.why_now: The 2026 Iran-war energy shock displaced workers, and ageing economies are widening visa routes for care and trades.
ideas.revenue_model: $1.5-3k employer placement fee per worker, plus employer-paid training subscriptions.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Displaced migrants are a supply shock nobody is organising. Employer-pays recruitment is both ethical and the direction of ILO fair-recruitment rules.
ideas.first_30_days: Sign one Kerala training institute and one overseas care-home operator, and run 30 candidates through a pilot.

ideas.title: App-Diet Service for the Phone-Upgrade Freeze
ideas.one_liner: As phones get unaffordable, today's handset becomes a five-year handset, so old-device performance decides who keeps users.
ideas.customer: Banks, wallets, telcos and government digital services with large user bases on 2-3GB RAM Android phones in Africa, India and LatAm.
ideas.problem: Memory-driven price rises are stretching replacement cycles. Bloated apps crash on old devices, and churn from that is invisible in analytics.
ideas.solution: A fixed-price audit on a real farm of used 2GB phones on 2G/3G. Deliver sub-10MB lite builds and WhatsApp or USSD fallbacks, then a monthly regression retainer. The wedge is a four-week audit for one mid-tier bank or wallet.
ideas.why_now: Memory is 30-40% of phone cost, LatAm shipments fell 10%, and GSMA's $40 phone pilot shows the price problem.
ideas.revenue_model: $15-40k per audit and $5-10k per month for device-lab monitoring.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Everyone forecasts the next phone. The second-order effect is that the current phone lasts far longer, so performance on old hardware, not features, drives retention.
ideas.first_30_days: Buy 15 used phones and publish a teardown of the top 10 fintech apps in Nigeria or India. Use it to book audits.

ideas.title: Zero-Commission Motor Third-Party Renewal Rails
ideas.one_liner: If motor third-party pays agents 0%, nobody sells the mandatory cover, so insurers need a cost-plus renewal utility.
ideas.customer: Indian general insurers, especially public-sector ones, and fleet owners; insurers pay a per-renewal fee.
ideas.problem: The IRDAI draft (Sep 23) cuts commission caps from 30% to 20%, sets 0% on motor third-party and 5% on own-damage. PB Fintech fell 36% in a day, and agents and aggregators lose any reason to chase mandatory renewals.
ideas.solution: Automated renewal reminders using expiry data from dealers and registration records, sent as WhatsApp messages in local languages with UPI payment. Charge a flat servicing fee. The wedge is two-wheeler third-party renewals in one state for one insurer.
ideas.why_now: The draft is out for comment now, and insurers must find distribution that costs less than commission.
ideas.revenue_model: Rs 30-80 per renewal from the insurer, with own-damage upsell.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: When distribution stops paying, a mandatory product needs a utility rather than a marketplace, and the underwriter is the natural buyer. The draft could change, so build for both outcomes.
ideas.first_30_days: Pitch three insurers. Run a 5,000-vehicle renewal test using expiry lists from a dealer network.

ideas.title: Payroll-Deducted Paylater Refinance for Factory Workers
ideas.one_liner: Consolidate minimum-wage workers' paylater and online loans into one payroll-deducted instalment, sold to the employer as retention.
ideas.customer: Indonesian manufacturers and retailers with 1,000+ minimum-wage staff, especially in Java's industrial belts; employers pay a fee and a partner lender funds.
ideas.problem: Paylater financing reached Rp43.28T in May and online lending Rp100.69T, and defaults are rising among minimum-wage workers. Collection harassment causes absenteeism and turnover.
ideas.solution: Consolidate a worker's paylater and pinjol debts into one lower-rate loan repaid via payroll, funded by a licensed multifinance or bank partner. The wedge is three factories in Bekasi and Karawang.
ideas.why_now: OJK scrutiny is rising and the 2026 macro squeeze is pushing defaults up.
ideas.revenue_model: 1-2% origination plus lender spread share, and an employer fee of Rp10-15k per worker per month.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The paylater trap is an HR problem before it is a credit problem, and the employer is the only party with payroll access and a reason to care.
ideas.first_30_days: Interview HR heads at three factories and pilot with 200 workers using a partner lender.

ideas.title: GST Credit Recovery on UPI Fees
ideas.one_liner: Recover the 18% GST on new UPI MDR fees as input credit for retailers and distributors that will otherwise never claim it.
ideas.customer: GST-registered mobile, FMCG and pharma retailers and distributors in India, and their chartered accountants.
ideas.problem: From Oct 15 the 0.4% MDR carries 18% GST, and AICPDF estimates a Rs 7,000-9,000 Cr burden on distributors. Small businesses will not reconcile bulk PSP fee invoices to GSTR-2B, so credit is left unclaimed.
ideas.solution: Ingest PSP settlement reports, match fee invoices to GSTR-2B, flag missing credits and produce claim workpapers for CAs. Composition-scheme dealers are ineligible and must be screened out. The wedge is retailer associations already mobilising over the fee.
ideas.why_now: MDR starts Oct 15 and retailer bodies are organised around a 'No UPI Day' on Oct 2.
ideas.revenue_model: 10-15% of recovered credit, or Rs 499-1,999 per month per business.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The protest is about the 0.4%. The GST layer is partly recoverable money nobody is discussing, and associations will trade it for a visible win for members.
ideas.first_30_days: Build reconciliation for PhonePe and Paytm settlement file formats and sign two retailer associations.

ideas.title: Withholding-Credit Reconciliation for Indonesian Sellers
ideas.one_liner: Reconcile marketplace-withheld tax against annual returns for the many small sellers across Shopee, TikTok Shop and Tokopedia.
ideas.customer: Indonesian SME marketplace sellers and the bookkeepers who serve them.
ideas.problem: Indonesia starts marketplace tax collection on Oct 1 and has cut de minimis to $3. Sellers on several platforms will see withheld amounts on payouts, and matching those to annual filings creates over- and under-payment risk.
ideas.solution: Ingest payout statements and withholding proofs by API or WhatsApp forward, reconcile per platform, flag threshold crossings and generate return workpapers. The wedge is a white-label tool for accountants who serve seller communities.
ideas.why_now: The Oct 1 start date forces this pain within a quarter. Details of the rules should be verified before building.
ideas.revenue_model: Rp99-299k per month per seller, or an accountant white-label licence.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Platform collection makes compliance visible, and a seller's first pain is reconciling rather than filing. The accountant channel is fragmented and unserved.
ideas.first_30_days: Support one platform's statement format and recruit 50 sellers through seller WhatsApp groups.

ideas.title: Customs Broker-as-Software for LatAm Micro-Importers
ideas.one_liner: Tariff walls turn Temu-era resellers into importers, so sell them classification, duty prepayment and pre-filed declarations.
ideas.customer: Parcel consolidators and micro-importers in Mexico and Argentina, and courier forwarders serving them.
ideas.problem: Temu has 105M LatAm monthly users, Mexico charges 33.5% on parcels and Argentina proposes a 30% duty. Resellers now face classification, valuation and tax questions, and brokers charge per-entry fees that kill small shipments.
ideas.solution: An HS-code classifier, duty calculator, pre-filed declaration flow and duty prepayment float. The wedge is consolidators shipping 200-1,000 parcels a week from China.
ideas.why_now: Anti-parcel walls went up across LatAm in 2025-26, and Indonesia's de minimis cut shows the pattern spreading.
ideas.revenue_model: $2-5 per parcel plus 1-2% on duty financing.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Tariff walls do not kill cross-border demand, they create a compliance tax, and the seller of compliance wins on volume.
ideas.first_30_days: Partner with two forwarders and cover the 20 most common HS codes for their volume.

ideas.title: Gig Social-Security Compliance Engine for Mid-Size Platforms
ideas.one_liner: A four-week compliance package for India's long tail of aggregator platforms that cannot build labour-code tooling in-house.
ideas.customer: Indian home-services, logistics, ride and staffing platforms with 5k-100k gig workers.
ideas.problem: India's labour codes require aggregator contributions to a social security fund and worker registration. Over 20% of gig workers log 70+ hours a week, and the government forced platforms to drop 10-minute branding in Jan 2026. Founders bear the audit exposure.
ideas.solution: e-Shram registration sync, contribution computation, hours-worked flags and worker benefit statements. The wedge is a fixed-fee readiness audit and setup for logistics and home-service platforms.
ideas.why_now: Labour codes are now in force, enforcement is starting, and quick-commerce attrition (51% at Zepto) pushes platforms to show worker-welfare records.
ideas.revenue_model: Rs 10-30 per worker per month plus a setup fee.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Large platforms build in-house. The 500 mid-size platforms cannot, and they have real budgets because penalties land on founders.
ideas.first_30_days: Run free readiness audits for 10 platforms and refine the contribution calculation with a labour-law firm partner.

ideas.title: Solar Battery Warranty-Claim Recovery Desk
ideas.one_liner: Pool failed-battery claims from small African installers and enforce them against Chinese manufacturers for a share of recovered value.
ideas.customer: Solar installers and importers in Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana and South Africa holding failed batteries and inverters.
ideas.problem: Africa has imported more battery dollars than panels from China since 2024. Cheap packs fail, and claims need serial verification, BMS logs, RMA logistics and language skills, so installers absorb the losses.
ideas.solution: A claims desk that captures failure evidence by QR and app, files with OEMs, consolidates returns and tracks credit notes. The wedge is five Lagos importers with a backlog of dead units.
ideas.why_now: The battery import surge of 2024-26 is now reaching failure age, and installer margins are compressing.
ideas.revenue_model: 15-25% of recovered value, moving to SaaS plus failure-data sales to insurers.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: A warranty is worth only what you can enforce. Batching many small buyers gives leverage over OEMs and produces failure data that insurers need.
ideas.first_30_days: Collect backlog lists from three importers and file the first 100 claims.

ideas.title: Farmer-Photo Crop Insurance Verification
ideas.one_liner: Replace satellite guesswork with dense, fraud-checked farmer photos, read by locally trained crop models, to trigger insurance payouts.
ideas.customer: Agricultural insurers and reinsurers, agri-input companies and cooperatives in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.
ideas.problem: Western models fail spectacularly on African crops, index insurance has high basis risk, and manual claim verification costs more than a smallholder premium.
ideas.solution: A local crop-damage model trained on image datasets (one project has 5M+ crop images) that takes geo-tagged WhatsApp photos, cross-checks neighbouring farms and weather, and triggers mobile-money payouts. The wedge is one maize or coffee cooperative with one insurer.
ideas.why_now: Local crop datasets and small on-device models exist now, and FarmerChat has answered 8M+ farmer questions, so farmers already talk to AI on their phones.
ideas.revenue_model: $0.50-2 per policy per season for verification, or a share of premium.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Basis risk is solved by dense ground truth from the insured themselves, not by better satellites.
ideas.first_30_days: Partner with a cooperative of about 2,000 farmers and run photo verification in parallel with existing claims for one season.

ideas.title: Savings-Group Credit Score and Treasury
ideas.one_liner: Turn informal savings groups into a credit bureau and stablecoin treasury that asset financiers can lend against.
ideas.customer: Financiers of productive assets (solar irrigation, motorbikes, milk coolers) and NGOs, with savings groups as end users.
ideas.problem: Sandi AI already reaches 10,000+ farmer groups that buy solar irrigation from pooled savings rather than loans. Chamas, VSLAs, tandas and arisan have no records that lenders can see.
ideas.solution: A WhatsApp and USSD ledger that logs contributions and minutes, produces a group credit history and optionally holds a stablecoin group treasury that diaspora members can top up. The wedge is selling qualified-group leads to asset financiers.
ideas.why_now: Kenya and Nigeria are legitimising stablecoins, local-language voice models can log minutes, and Sandi AI has shown demand.
ideas.revenue_model: $20-60 per funded asset lead, plus a 0.5% treasury fee.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The group is the unit of trust in informal finance. Digitising it creates a bureau that cannot be scraped from mobile money data.
ideas.first_30_days: Sign 100 groups in Kenya through one NGO and record three months of contributions to prove predictive value.

ideas.title: Charged Battery Cylinders for Market Traders
ideas.one_liner: Deliver and swap standardised 2 kWh LFP packs daily to market traders, the way gas cylinders are sold.
ideas.customer: Market traders, salons, food vendors and phone-charging kiosks in Lagos, Kano, Nairobi and Accra.
ideas.problem: These businesses run petrol and diesel generators or lose sales in outages, and cannot afford upfront batteries even as Africa imports more battery dollars than panels.
ideas.solution: Rugged handled LFP packs, solar-charged at rooftop depots and swapped daily by motorcycle couriers on a per-swap subscription. The wedge is 200 vendors around one market served from a depot with about 60 packs.
ideas.why_now: LFP cell prices are low, the fuel-price shock hurts generator users, and distributed solar is already scaling faster than utility supply.
ideas.revenue_model: $0.80-1.50 per swap, with 30-40% gross margin at about 70% pack utilisation.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Small traders buy energy the way they buy gas, in small frequent delivered units. A swap network amortises battery cost across many users and removes the upfront barrier.
ideas.first_30_days: Build 30 packs and run swaps for 20 vendors at one market to measure utilisation and pack cycle life.

ideas.title: Cross-Border Income Passport for Freelancers
ideas.one_liner: Give stablecoin-paid remote workers a verifiable, portable income record that landlords, lenders and visa agents accept.
ideas.customer: Freelancers and remote workers in Nigeria, the Philippines, Colombia and Kenya; landlords, lenders and visa agents pay to verify.
ideas.problem: Freelancers cannot get portable income records for loans or visas, and stablecoin and platform-wallet earnings leave no bank paper trail.
ideas.solution: Connect wallets, payout platforms and invoices, then produce signed income attestations with a QR verification link. The wedge is rental and visa income letters at about $15 each for remote workers in Lagos and Manila.
ideas.why_now: Stablecoin payroll and invoicing tools like Bloccpay are spreading, Flutterwave and Yellow Card are scaling, and LatAm lenders are hunting for new borrowers.
ideas.revenue_model: $10-20 per attestation, plus $1-3 per verification call from lenders.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck in stablecoin income is proving it, not moving it. Whoever gets accepted by three lenders becomes a bureau for the remote-work diaspora.
ideas.first_30_days: Build attestations from Payoneer, Wise and USDC statements and test with 50 workers and one landlord network.

ideas.title: Consumer-Side Debt Negotiation Agent for Brazil
ideas.one_liner: A WhatsApp agent that reads a household's Open Finance data and negotiates all its debts on the debtor's behalf.
ideas.customer: Over-indebted Brazilian households, paying a success fee.
ideas.problem: Household debt is around 82% by the cited indicator, delinquency is at a record, and Lula's Sep 25 relief may reach under 1% of defaults. People face many creditors and rarely know discounts are available.
ideas.solution: With consent, pull debts from Open Finance, build a repayment plan, negotiate through lender collection channels and debt portals, and set up Pix Automatico debits. The wedge is revolving card debt and overdraft for low-income users.
ideas.why_now: Open Finance and Pix Automatico are mature and LLM agents can now negotiate reliably. The online betting ban leaves ex-bettors with debts and no plan.
ideas.revenue_model: 10-15% of the discount obtained, charged only on success.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Existing collections platforms are lender-paid and optimise recovery. A debtor-side agent exposes rate arbitrage and gives lenders a rational counterparty at scale.
ideas.first_30_days: Run a concierge pilot with 100 users, using humans plus AI drafting, to learn discount rates by lender. Check consumer-protection rules first.

ideas.title: Install Clubs: Brazilian Consórcio for Home Contractors
ideas.one_liner: A contractor-anchored, interest-free buying pool: 60-200 homeowners pay monthly into escrow and each month a few move up the queue (by draw or bid) to get their roof, heat pump or solar+battery installed.
ideas.customer: Independent home-service contractors (roofing, HVAC/heat pump, solar+storage, windows) with 5-50 staff who want pre-sold backlog. Their end users are homeowners who have been quoted $8-20k and don't want a 9-12% HELOC or home-improvement loan.
ideas.problem: Big-ticket home upgrades stall on financing. Contractors burn 10-20% of revenue on lead gen and lose many quoted jobs because the homeowner can't or won't borrow. The 25C/25D federal credits ended for installs after Dec 31, 2025, so the effective price jumped overnight.
ideas.solution: Software + bank escrow + a lawyer-drafted prepaid-service template that lets a contractor run a 'club' for one product (e.g., a $9k heat-pump install). Members pay $100-200/month into segregated escrow. Every month one or more members are allocated an install by lottery or by bidding extra to jump the queue. The contractor is the counterparty and delivers at a locked price, so there is no loan and no interest. The platform earns an administration fee instead of interest, as Brazilian consórcios do.
ideas.why_now: Brazil's consórcio system hit a record 12.76M active participants and about R$500B of credit sold in 2025, in a high-rate environment, so the model is proven when loans are expensive. In the US the 25C/25D credits vanished on Dec 31, 2025, rates are still high, and the only consórcio-style player I found (NWX) sells general credit letters for real estate and vehicles. Nobody has wrapped the pool around a service the seller delivers.
ideas.revenue_model: Administration fee of roughly 8-12% of contract value collected in monthly installments, a SaaS fee per contractor club, and a share of escrow float yield.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: A consórcio is not a loan, it is a queue with a price guarantee. Making the licensed contractor the counterparty turns the pool into a prepaid-service escrow (like layaway) instead of a credit product, which sidesteps most lending regulation. The contractor gets what it wants most: scheduled backlog, cash before work, and near-zero CAC because 'your neighbor's roof gets done this month' recruits the next member. Homeowners who were declined or scared off by loans are the fastest-filling segment.
ideas.first_30_days: Sign 2-3 contractors in one state. Get an escrow account at a community bank and a prepaid-service agreement drafted by a lawyer who knows that state's home-improvement deposit rules. Mine each contractor's list of past quotes that never closed and pre-enroll about 40 members in a 'Founders Club' at about $150/month for a $9k install. Run the first allocation in month 2, so the first installed job and first admin-fee revenue land by around day 60.

ideas.title: Landing Fund: Sweden's Layoff Council for US Employers
ideas.one_liner: Employers pay about 0.3% of payroll into a pooled transition fund that gives every laid-off employee case management, retraining money and bridge pay, so companies can restructure without severance drama.
ideas.customer: CFOs and CHROs at 200-3,000-employee US companies (software, fintech, insurance, BPO, media) that are restructuring around AI or expect to. Reached through PEOs, HR brokers and benefits consultants.
ideas.problem: US severance is ad hoc (about 12-14 weeks for white-collar staff) and outplacement is usually a webinar. Leaders delay or botch layoffs because there is no humane, pre-agreed answer to 'what happens to the people we cut.' One tracker counts roughly 205,000 AI-attributed US layoffs through August 2026, concentrated in entry-level and back-office roles.
ideas.solution: A US version of Sweden's Trygghetsrådet (TRR). Employers join a pool at a set percentage of payroll. When someone is laid off they get a named case manager, retraining vouchers, a 2-4 month bridge-pay top-up, and a COBRA/health bridge subsidy, with providers paid partly on outcomes. Employers get a standard offboarding playbook, smaller bespoke severance, and less litigation and survivor-morale damage. Launch as prepaid 'transition credits' (no insurance license needed) and graduate to a captive or reinsured product.
ideas.why_now: AI became the top stated reason for corporate job cuts in the spring of 2026, entry-level white-collar hiring has collapsed, and executives are being publicly punished for how they lay people off. In Sweden the model covers 30,000+ companies and about 700,000 employees on 0.3% of payroll, and roughly 9 in 10 active clients found work, study or self-employment within seven months (2019 figures).
ideas.revenue_model: Per-employee-per-month or a percentage of payroll (0.2-0.4%). Unspent reserves fund the next cohort, with margin on training-partner rev share and, later, insurance float.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Sweden's system works because employers fund it collectively, so no single firm carries the full cost of a big layoff, and that pooling turns a dreaded cost into a predictable premium. The buyer's real pain is decision speed and reputation, not the money. A ready-made, respected answer to 'what about the people' lets an executive act faster and more humanely, which is why the product can sell before any regulator asks for it.
ideas.first_30_days: Build a 'layoff readiness pack' (offboarding checklist, manager scripts, fund terms) and pitch 15 mid-size companies through two PEOs and an HR consultancy. Line up two training providers and one career-coaching group. Target letters of intent from 5-10 founding employers covering about 5,000 employees at roughly $15 per employee per month, with a first paying pool by month 3.

ideas.title: Silver Crews: Retiree Work Co-ops for US Towns
ideas.one_liner: A membership co-op for retirees 62+ that contracts with towns, school districts and HOAs for short, insured, daytime jobs (crossing guards, school and library aides, grounds work, event staffing) and acts as employer of record.
ideas.customer: Municipal public-works and parks departments, school districts, libraries, HOAs and property managers who pay per job-hour. Retirees join as members.
ideas.problem: Employers with 5-15 hour-a-week daytime needs can't hire for them. Retirees want flexible, meaningful part-time work but distrust app gigs and can't easily get liability and accident cover. A record 4.18M Americans turned 65 in 2025, crossing guards are already the most senior-dominated occupation (nearly 1 in 3 are 65+), and about 15% of retirees say they'd consider returning to paid work.
ideas.solution: A county-level 'Silver Crew' modeled on Japan's Silver Human Resource Centers (about 1,300 centers, 700,000+ members). It recruits, background-checks and trains 200-400 members, holds standing contracts, schedules shifts, runs payroll (W-2 or contract), carries pooled workers'-comp/accident insurance, and hosts a monthly social meetup. Customers get a reliable pool without hiring headaches, and members get a community as well as a paycheck.
ideas.why_now: Peak 65 will stay elevated through at least 2027, school and municipal labor shortages persist, and municipal budgets favor contracting over adding headcount. Japan's centers have proven the model over decades, while US equivalents are small nonprofit senior-employment programs, not service-contract businesses.
ideas.revenue_model: Mark-up of roughly 15-25% on member pay billed to customers, small annual member dues, and margin on pooled insurance.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The scarce input isn't retiree labor, it's the wrapper. A town can't onboard a 68-year-old for six hours a week, but a co-op with pooled accident cover, one background-check process and a single invoice can. Japanese centers work because the arrangement is legally a contract for a task, not a job, which strips out friction. The social meetup is the retention engine, and it is what makes seniors choose this over Uber or DoorDash.
ideas.first_30_days: Pick one retiree-dense county (Florida, Arizona or a New England town). Sign 3 pilot contracts (an HOA, a school district and a library) using an existing PEO for payroll and workers' comp. Recruit 40 retirees through senior centers, churches and Nextdoor. Run the first paid shifts within 4 weeks and invoice monthly.

ideas.title: Dr. Simi USA: Pharmacy-Plus-Consult for the Uninsured
ideas.one_liner: Small-format, generic-first pharmacies with a nurse-practitioner consult room beside the counter, posted cash prices and no insurance needed, following Mexico's Farmacias Similares model and landing in US pharmacy deserts.
ideas.customer: Uninsured and underinsured adults in pharmacy deserts and immigrant neighborhoods. An estimated 4.8M Americans lost coverage after the enhanced ACA subsidies expired, and about 48M people live in pharmacy deserts. The second customer is at-risk independent pharmacists who license the clinic kit.
ideas.problem: Rite Aid is gone (all stores closed after its 2025 Chapter 11), Walgreens is shrinking, and independents are squeezed by PBM reimbursement. An uninsured person with a UTI or sinus infection faces a $150-250 urgent-care visit plus retail drug prices, so many just skip treatment.
ideas.solution: An 800-1,200 sq ft store or a 200 sq ft conversion inside an existing independent pharmacy. A flat $25-40 NP consult (loss leader), point-of-care tests (strep, flu, UTI, A1c), on-site dispensing of generics at transparent cost-plus prices, bilingual staff, and chronic-refill programs. The visit and the dispense happen in one 10-minute stop, so there is no abandoned prescription. Mexico's Farmacias Similares runs thousands of outlets with an attached doctor's office charging a few dollars.
ideas.why_now: Coverage is shrinking at the same time as pharmacy access: enhanced ACA subsidies lapsed at the end of 2025, Medicaid cuts phase in through 2026-27, and Rite Aid's liquidation left holes in low-income neighborhoods. Cost Plus Drugs has taught Americans to expect transparent generic prices, so a cash-price store is no longer strange.
ideas.revenue_model: Dispensing margin on generics, flat consult fees, point-of-care lab fees, OTC sales, plus licensing or franchise fees for the turnkey clinic-in-a-pharmacy kit sold to independents.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Don't compete with telehealth on convenience; win on adjacency. Consult plus dispense in one stop removes the biggest leak in cash-pay care, which is people who get a prescription and never fill it. The fastest route isn't building stores at all. It is converting existing independents on the edge of closure by giving them a second revenue line, and an already-licensed pharmacy removes months of setup.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit 3 independent pharmacies in Latino neighborhoods (Texas, Florida or Illinois). Contract per-diem NPs under a collaborative practice agreement, build a 100 sq ft consult room, and print a simple price list ('$29 visit, $4 generics'). Market through WhatsApp groups, churches and community radio. Run a 60-day pilot and track visit-to-fill conversion and margin per visit.

ideas.title: Common Rooms: Community-Share Buyouts of Neighborhood Bars
ideas.one_liner: A studio that helps retiring owners sell beloved bars, cafes, bookstores and cinemas to hundreds of neighbors through community-share offers, then supplies a manager and shared back office.
ideas.customer: Owners over 60 of profitable independent third-place businesses who can't find a buyer, plus neighbors who buy $100-500 shares. Commercial landlords are a third stakeholder.
ideas.problem: Boomers own most main-street businesses and many will simply close, because a qualified buyer with SBA-loan credit is rare. Communities lose their remaining third places while loneliness is a public-health issue.
