ideas.revenue_model: Pharma subscriptions of $60-250k per product family per year. Insurer analytics contracts of $50-150k per year. Custom post-marketing studies at $100-300k. A free public tier drives owner-reported data.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Companion-animal medicine is the last big therapeutic area with no Sentinel-style system, and insurers are the only long-lived holders of cross-clinic data. After a public safety scare, drugmakers will pay for credibility that they cannot generate themselves, and insurers will pay for the same data to reduce claims.
ideas.first_30_days: Pitch small MGAs and startup insurers (hungry for analytics, less locked into data rules) on a free pilot in exchange for a data-sharing agreement. Build signal detection for the 10 most common drugs and biologics. Publish a public report on one hot topic, then sell two pharma safety leads a pilot subscription. Expect first revenue at month 4-6.

ideas.title: End-of-Life Pet Cell Banking via Aftercare Providers
ideas.angle: Pairing 2: Biotech tools/synbio/lab automation/AI drug discovery x Pets & animal health/vet shortage/pet insurance
ideas.one_liner: Sell a living-cell keepsake through pet crematories and euthanasia vets, and build a consented canine and feline cell-and-genome atlas for research.
ideas.customer: Grieving pet owners pay $249-399 per animal. Pet crematories, in-home euthanasia vets and cemeteries are distribution partners. Vet-pharma, AI-drug-discovery and academic groups license the consented, de-identified cell lines and genomes.
ideas.problem: Owners will pay for memorials, but the only 'living' option today is boutique cloning-linked gene banking at roughly $1,600+ that almost nobody hears about at the moment they need it. Aftercare providers touch millions of pets a year and have no biotech product. At the same time, AI-driven and vet drug discovery lack breed-annotated cell lines and genomes tied to full medical histories, and proprietary biological datasets are commanding large valuations (Basecamp raised $140M; Tempus is assembling 100k genomes).
ideas.solution: A low-cost collection kit (skin punch biopsy in transport medium, chilled shipping) handled by a vet or trained aftercare staff within 24-48 hours of death. A contract lab establishes and cryopreserves fibroblast lines for 20+ years, and optional whole-genome sequencing is included. Owners choose 'keep only' or a discounted 'keep and donate to research'. Consented lines plus medical-record metadata go into a research atlas that partners license.
ideas.why_now: High-profile celebrity pet cloning in late 2025 made living pet genetics a mainstream conversation. Whole-genome sequencing now costs roughly $100-200, and proprietary datasets are what AI-bio investors pay for. Pet aftercare is a large, emotionally trusted channel that no biotech has approached, and vet-shortage-driven consolidation is pushing clinics toward add-on revenue.
ideas.revenue_model: $249-399 per animal plus $60 per year storage. Partners earn $40-60 per kit. Research licensing of consented lines and genomes at $500-2,000 per line with metadata, plus dataset subscriptions. Unit costs are about $120-180 for culture and cryostorage.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The scarce resource for pet biotech is not technology but trusted access to animals at the moment of death, and that access sits with crematories and euthanasia vets, not labs. Framing the purchase as optionality (cloning, future cell therapy) plus a donation option turns a grief moment into a data flywheel.
ideas.first_30_days: Contract an academic or commercial cell-banking lab for a validated tissue-to-line protocol. Sign 3-5 pet crematories or in-home euthanasia practices in one metro, and place 20 kits at a $99 introductory price. Recruit a supervising veterinarian and create an owner consent form covering research use. Take the first 30-50 lines to two vet-pharma or AI-biotech prospects for a data pilot.

ideas.title: Bank-Accepted $1,500 Diligence for Main Street Deals
ideas.angle: Pairing 1: SMB back office/compliance/marketing/succession x Trust & verification markets (succession x audits)
ideas.one_liner: A fixed-price, CPA-signed mini quality-of-earnings pack that brokers attach to sub-$1M business listings so SBA lenders and first-time buyers can close deals that currently die at diligence.
ideas.customer: Business brokers listing $150K-$1M cash-flow businesses (pay about $995 per listing to pre-certify), first-time individual buyers (pay $1,500 at letter of intent), and community-bank SBA lenders who accept the format.
ideas.problem: Boomer-owned Main Street businesses (HVAC, laundromats, landscaping, small clinics) sell on seller-supplied P&Ls and add-backs because a real quality-of-earnings review costs roughly $15K-50K (prior knowledge), which is more than many deals can bear. Search-fund capital targets $5-50M companies, so no formal capital or diligence product exists below $1M (brief inference). Deals die late or close on bad numbers.
ideas.solution: A five-day standardized pack. AI ties out bank feeds, POS data and sales-tax filings to IRS tax transcripts (hard to forge), samples add-backs, checks customer and revenue concentration, runs a reviews-and-traffic authenticity check (bought reviews and followers inflate perceived brand value), scans liens, licenses and litigation, and produces an owner-dependence score. A partner CPA reviews and signs. The signed pack attaches to the listing and is reusable across buyers.
ideas.why_now: SBA loosened acquisition financing on 2026-07-04 (7(a) and 504 loans can be combined for up to $10M of SBA-backed financing). AI-forged P&Ls and bank-statement PDFs are now trivial to produce (prior knowledge), so lenders and buyers need evidence that survives forgery. CPA supply is flat at about 678K, so cheap AI tie-out plus a reviewing CPA is the only way to serve small deals. Bench's Dec 2024 collapse showed sellers' books can be trapped inside a vendor.
ideas.revenue_model: $1,500 buyer-paid report or $995 broker pre-certification per listing, plus a $250 lender-portal fee. Roughly 3 CPA hours per pack plus software gives about 65% gross margin.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The deal-killer is not the price of diligence, it is that diligence gets redone for every buyer. Certifying the listing once turns a per-buyer cost into a per-listing asset that brokers will pay for because it buys deal certainty. Tax transcripts plus bank feeds are also the only evidence AI cannot cheaply fake.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit 3 freelance ex-QoE CPAs and ask 5 regional business brokers for active listings. Run 10 free packs in exchange for case studies and lender feedback, then charge $995 per listing. Walk the format past 2 SBA Preferred Lenders at community banks so 'lender-accepted' is true by month 3.

ideas.title: Random-Sample CPA Audits of AI Bookkeeping
ideas.angle: Pairing 1: SMB back office/compliance/marketing/succession x Trust & verification markets (bookkeeping x independent assurance)
ideas.one_liner: A $79/month independent assurance layer where a licensed CPA reviews a random sample of a micro-business's AI-categorized transactions and signs a monthly accuracy attestation backed by a penalty-reimbursement guarantee.
ideas.customer: Nonemployers and 1-10 employee businesses (contractors, salons, restaurants, e-commerce sellers) using AI bookkeeping in QuickBooks, Xero or startup tools. Secondary buyers are AI-bookkeeping vendors wanting white-label certification and lenders wanting attested books.
ideas.problem: 46% of AI-using small firms name accuracy as their top problem (Fed SBCS 2026). Intuit and Xero are pushing LLM categorization to millions of users, and Bench's Dec 2024 collapse locked customers out of their books for days. Owners find errors only at a tax bill, a loan denial or a penalty, and new OBBBA reporting (tips and overtime, the $2,000 1099 floor) raises the cost of misclassification.
ideas.solution: Stratified sampling weighted toward high-dollar, first-seen-vendor and deduction-sensitive transactions. The CPA confirms against receipts and bank data, fixes errors inside the customer's own software, and issues a monthly signed 'books verified' report with a measured error rate. A small reserve (later insurer-backed) reimburses penalties traceable to verified periods. Every attestation exports to a portable audit file that survives any vendor failing.
ideas.why_now: Mass-market LLM bookkeeping arrived in 2026 (Intuit-Anthropic and Xero-Anthropic partnerships) just as CPA headcount stalled near 678K. Intuit cut 17% of staff while opening about 600 offices, which signals that pure-AI trust is unsolved. No incumbent can credibly sell independent assurance on its own output.
ideas.revenue_model: $79/month per business with reviewer cost of roughly $15-25/month after AI triage. Add $2-5K/year white-label fees from AI bookkeepers, lender attestation fees, and warranty margin once insurer-backed.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Checking is roughly ten times cheaper than doing, so scarce CPAs can serve 10x more clients as auditors of samples than as preparers. Auditors must be independent of the producer, a position structurally closed to Intuit and Xero. The accumulated error-rate data by tool becomes a Consumer Reports-style asset that the vendors cannot publish themselves.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit 5 part-time or retired CPAs and sign 20 founding clients at $49 from contractor and salon-owner communities. Run a blind test of three AI bookkeepers on 50 anonymized sets of books and publish the error rates for press. Pitch 3 small bookkeeping firms to resell the attestation.

ideas.title: Contingency Refunds for Fake Local-Service Leads
ideas.angle: Pairing 1: SMB back office/compliance/marketing/succession x Trust & verification markets (local marketing x proving human/quality)
ideas.one_liner: A win-based service that audits what plumbers, HVAC firms, locksmiths, law offices and clinics pay per lead or call, proves which were bots, spam or out-of-area, and files the platform disputes owners never get around to.
ideas.customer: Owner-operators of 1-20 person home-service, legal and clinic businesses spending $1.5K-15K/month on Google Local Services Ads, Thumbtack, Angi, Yelp and tracked call numbers. Fee is 25% of credits recovered.
ideas.problem: 'Reaching customers' is the number-one small-business challenge (Fed SBCS 2026) while legacy local-marketing vendors shrink (Thryv 2025 revenue $785M, down). Owners pay per lead but cannot tell real jobs from junk, and platform dispute windows are short and evidence-heavy, so credits likely go unclaimed (my inference; recovery rates need testing). Bot share of web traffic is estimated anywhere from about 20% (Cloudflare CEO) to over 50% (Imperva/Fortune), and cheap AI voice agents make robo-calls to paid numbers easier.
ideas.solution: The owner connects ad and lead accounts or forwards lead emails and call-tracking numbers. The system transcribes calls, scores caller numbers, checks geography and duplicates, classifies wrong-service and spam leads, and flags synthetic voices. It assembles evidence and files disputes inside each platform's window, reconciles the credits, and reports a monthly verified-lead rate per channel to guide budget.
ideas.why_now: Speech-to-text and classification now cost pennies per call. AI-generated traffic is polluting pay-per-lead channels while platform-native verification stays thin. Small owners have less time and money than ever, and outcome-priced recovery is exactly what subscription incumbents cannot easily offer.
ideas.revenue_model: 25% of credits recovered, plus a $49/month scorecard after month 3. Later add white-label to marketing agencies and sell verified-lead-rate benchmarks.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Platforms already built refund mechanisms and profit from friction, so packaging evidence on time is the whole product. The independent verified-lead rate per channel is the first honest ROI data most SMBs ever get, and it may end up worth more than the refunds. Contingency pricing works because credits appear as visible cash in the ad account.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit 15 owners from HVAC, garage-door, locksmith and plumber Facebook groups with a free 60-day lookback audit. Contract VAs to file disputes manually and measure recovery as a percent of spend. Publish a junk-lead-rate benchmark by platform, and build software only once recovery exceeds roughly 8% of spend.

ideas.title: Recovering Tariff Surcharges Small Buyers Already Paid
ideas.angle: Pairing 1: SMB back office/compliance/marketing/succession x Trust & verification markets (compliance recovery x forensic audit)
ideas.one_liner: Contingency-fee forensic audits of supplier invoices that find the explicit 'tariff surcharge' lines small retailers, contractors and restaurants paid in 2025, and turn them into evidence packets while importers hold the refund money.
ideas.customer: Small retailers, contractors, restaurants, salons and small manufacturers that bought from distributors who itemized tariff surcharges. Fee is about 25% of recovery. Secondary customers are mid-size distributors that received IEEPA refunds and want a defensible pass-through rebate calculation.
ideas.problem: The Supreme Court ruled on 2026-02-20 that IEEPA does not authorize tariffs. CBP says about $166B is refundable to 330,000+ importers of record, with about $81B paid by July 2026. 76% of firms that source internationally passed costs to customers, so downstream small buyers paid the tax and get nothing directly (brief inference). Brokers and trade lawyers chase the importer's refund, not the payer's claim.
ideas.solution: The owner forwards a supplier-invoice mailbox or QuickBooks export. Document AI extracts surcharge lines and products, identifies the likely importer of record, calculates the claim, and packages evidence (invoice, surcharge wording, date, refund status) into a demand letter. A partner consumer-protection or commercial firm handles aggregated claims and arbitration. Distributors get an audit-trailed rebate module for voluntary pass-through.
ideas.why_now: The refund flow is happening now (CAPE launched by April 2026, 2,000+ suits filed), importers hold the cash, and downstream invoice records and claim windows decay every month. Document AI makes invoice-level extraction cheap. The IEEPA ruling is a one-time event, so the window is finite.
ideas.revenue_model: 25% contingency on recovered amounts, split with counsel. Add SaaS fees from distributors for rebate audits.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Explicit surcharge line items are invoice-level admissions that the charge existed to cover a tax later refunded, which makes these claims far stronger than generic price-increase complaints. Distributors want to keep small customers, so a clean evidence packet often converts to a negotiated credit without litigation. Claim strength varies by contract and state and needs counsel, so the business is forensic evidence assembly, not legal advice.
ideas.first_30_days: Build the invoice parser on 50 sample invoices and offer free surcharge scans to 30 members of one trade association (independent hardware, bike or restaurant-supply buyers). Identify the 10 most frequent surcharging distributors, sign a contingency-split agreement with a law firm, and target first negotiated credits by month 3.

ideas.title: Bookkeeper-Run Payee Registry Against Invoice Fraud
ideas.angle: Pairing 1: SMB back office/compliance/marketing/succession x Trust & verification markets (back office x reputation network)
ideas.one_liner: Independent bookkeeping firms pool hashed vendor bank-account confirmations into a shared registry that flags fake invoices and 'new bank details' fraud at tiny businesses, then grows into a portable payment-reputation file for thin-file borrowers.
ideas.customer: Fractional bookkeeping and CFO firms serving 30-300 micro-clients ($99-500/month per firm). Later buyers are wholesalers, equipment lessors and CDFI lenders paying $3-8 per reputation pull.
ideas.problem: US payments lack payee-name verification (the UK has Confirmation of Payee; prior knowledge). AI writes flawless fake invoices and clones voices, as in Arup's roughly $25M deepfake video-call loss. Nacha's 2026 rules push originators toward risk-based fraud monitoring (prior knowledge; verify). Each bookkeeper sees only their own clients, so nobody learns from anyone else's near-miss. Separately, 22% of small firms seeking credit got nothing and solo businesses have no trade-reference file.
ideas.solution: A browser extension and API for bill-pay tools that hashes vendor name plus routing plus account and checks the registry: confirmed by N firms, flag first-time changes, and force a call-back to an independently sourced number. Confirmed payment events (on time, disputed) accrue to a per-business reputation file the owner controls and can carry between bookkeepers.
ideas.why_now: Voice cloning and AI-written invoices make payment fraud cheap. PE roll-ups of accounting firms push big players upmarket, so independent bookkeepers need shared infrastructure to compete. Bench's collapse made portability a selling point. The higher 1099 floor ($2,000 from 2026) likely means fewer W-9 and TIN collections, degrading vendor hygiene (inference).
ideas.revenue_model: $99-500/month per firm, per-pull fees from lenders and suppliers, and a revenue share back to contributing firms.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Fraud data is a network good that big vendors cannot pool across rival software stacks, but a neutral consortium of small firms can, the way independent pharmacies and hardware stores formed co-ops. Bookkeepers already perform informal KYB on every client, so the registry monetizes knowledge they already hold.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit 10 bookkeeping firms through a bookkeeper association or Facebook groups. Run a hashed shared registry manually (spreadsheet plus call-back desk) covering their combined 1,000+ vendors at $99/month. Record the first prevented fraud as the case study, then build the Bill.com and QuickBooks extension.

ideas.title: Public-Access TV Stations Become Media Notaries
ideas.angle: Pairing 2: Creator economy & media provenance x Government/public sector/defense/municipal services (human-made proof x municipal media infrastructure)
ideas.one_liner: Convert struggling PEG community-media centers into witnessed-recording and signing hubs that cities pay to certify official meeting video and creators pay to prove a recording was performed live by a human in a real room.
ideas.customer: City and county clerks ($300-600/month for signed, canonical video of meetings, hearings and emergency briefings), PEG access centers (keep about 60% as delivery partners), and local musicians, podcasters and hyperlocal news creators ($45 per witnessed session or $15/month for verified-clip embeds). Later buyers are sync buyers and ad agencies.
ideas.problem: PEG centers (public, educational and government access TV) are funded by cable franchise fees that erode as cable subscriptions fall (prior knowledge), yet they own studios, gear, staff and a role recording local government. Meanwhile fully AI tracks passed 50% of Deezer uploads (July 2026), AI-cloned officials' clips circulate, platform human badges are free and per-artist (Spotify) or absent (YouTube will not demote labeled AI), and detectors are only probabilistic. Nobody sells 'this was made live, in this room, on this date, witnessed by a public institution'.
ideas.solution: A roughly $600 witness kit plus software: hardware-signed capture into C2PA manifests, staff-attested session logs with an ID check of performers, and raw timestamped multitrack takes. Cities get a canonical signed meeting archive and a public 'verify this clip' page. Local news creators embed verified clips, and artists attach a 'Recorded live at [Center], [date]' credential to releases and distributor metadata.
ideas.why_now: EU AI Act Article 50 marking and disclosure duties started applying 2026-08-02. C2PA 2.3 and TikTok's July 2026 steering-committee entry mean signed media can now travel across platforms. Platforms went from tolerating to policing AI in months (Bandcamp ban, Spotify AI Persona labels, TIDAL demonetization), and PEG funding pressure means centers need new revenue lines.
ideas.revenue_model: City subscriptions, per-session fees split with PEG centers, an annual software license to centers, and later per-clip verification fees from sync buyers.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: A credential is only as trustworthy as the institution behind it. Platforms cannot referee because they sell AI tools, and detectors give probabilities while a witness gives testimony. PEG centers are the only neutral, government-adjacent, physically distributed and already-recording institutions in most towns, and their core asset is exactly what provenance lacks: a place and a person willing to attest.
ideas.first_30_days: Contact the Alliance for Community Media state chapters and equip 3 PEG stations in one state. Sign one month of council meetings free, then demo a deepfaked council clip against the signed original to sell a $300/month city plan. Open 'Witnessed Live' studio hours to 20 local artists at $45.

ideas.title: Deepfake Shields for Mayors, Sold Through Risk Pools
ideas.angle: Pairing 2: Creator economy & media provenance x Government/public sector/defense/municipal services (long-tail likeness protection x municipal risk channel)
ideas.one_liner: Long-tail likeness and voice protection for roughly 500,000 local elected officials, clerks and first responders who have no agency to police impersonation, sold as a loss-control service through municipal insurance risk pools and county election offices.
ideas.customer: State and regional municipal risk pools and cyber pools ($300-1,500 per member per year), county election offices ($500-2,000 each), and sheriffs' and police chiefs' associations.
ideas.problem: YouTube's likeness detection reached celebrities through CAA, UTA and WME in April 2026 with no path for anyone else, and voice clones need only seconds of audio (prior knowledge). Local officials are high-impact targets: a cloned 'mayor' telling finance staff to wire funds, fake curfew or polling-place notices, fake council videos. Local IT is thin (Dallas County is cutting 31 IT staff), federal election-security help to localities was scaled back in 2025 (prior knowledge), and the midterms are Nov 3, 2026.
ideas.solution: Enroll officials with consented voice and face references and monitor major platforms using existing detection APIs. Run a human takedown desk using platform impersonation policies and state deepfake statutes. Give finance staff call-back code-word protocols and quarterly voice-clone drills, and deliver evidence packs for insurers and police.
ideas.why_now: Midterm urgency, celebrity-only platform tools, and cheap high-quality voice cloning all arrive together. Pools face rising social-engineering claims (inference), and EU Article 50 plus platform enforcement raise expectations that impersonations get pulled quickly.
ideas.revenue_model: A per-member fee paid by the pool, per-incident takedown fees, drill fees, and premium credits negotiated with the pool.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The 'agency' that long-tail people lack is the insurance pool. It already pays social-engineering claims, has member-services budgets, and can buy for a thousand towns in one sale. Framing the product as claims reduction rather than reputation management is what unlocks the budget.
ideas.first_30_days: Interview 5 pool loss-control managers and sell a $499 election-season kit to 20 county clerks. Run a free voice-clone drill for one pool's treasurers association to produce a claim-reduction case study.

ideas.title: Independent Gauntlet for Police and Counter-Drone Buyers
ideas.angle: Pairing 2: Creator economy & media provenance x Government/public sector/defense/municipal services (creator-style trusted reviewer x dual-use municipal buyers)
ideas.one_liner: A buyer-funded, video-first test lab that flies and publishes open-protocol results on police first-responder drones and counter-drone detection, the way the Pentagon's public Gauntlets do for its own buyers, funded by agency subscriptions and never by vendors.
ideas.customer: Police, fire and emergency-management tech buyers at city and county agencies ($1,200-3,000 per agency-year for full data, vendor scorecards and RFP language), buyer consortia, and grant-funded counter-UAS programs (FEMA's $500M program, Dallas's $10M set-aside).
ideas.problem: Local buyers cannot audit vendors: state and local tech contracts average 7 years, only 5.3% of AI-relevant provisions address transparency, and GenAI-written RFPs make every proposal look perfect. Vendor claims are unreliable: only 24% of drones reached 10 km in the Pentagon's Gauntlet 1, Cape Canaveral's radars miss quadcopters, and 700+ drones were seized around one World Cup stadium. Trade media and cooperative marketplaces are vendor-funded, so independent performance data does not exist.
ideas.solution: Quarterly standardized tests covering range, wind, latency, false alarms against birds and RF clutter, and detection of cooperative test drones only (no jamming). Runs are recorded with signed telemetry and raw video so results cannot be disputed or edited, and protocols are open. Drone creators co-host as pilots and distribute the long-form video, while agencies pay for data, scorecards, sample RFP language and an ask-us desk. Vendors may buy re-tests only after results are public.
ideas.why_now: The Pentagon's public Gauntlets (Gauntlet 2 in Sept 2026: 23 platforms, 19 companies, 1,858 sorties) normalized head-to-head public testing. Counter-drone money is flowing to cities, sponsored and AI-written content swamps review media, and local surveillance-tech purchases now face public scrutiny.
ideas.revenue_model: Agency subscriptions, custom pre-procurement tests paid from grants, and paid training. No vendor sponsorship, which is the trust asset.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: DoD's Gauntlet works because the buyer controls the test. Local agencies have the same need but no lab budget, and the creator-media model (audience-funded, no sponsors) is exactly the structure that makes an independent lab self-sustaining. Vendor-funded trade media and vendor-listing marketplaces are structurally unable to be the referee.
ideas.first_30_days: Buy five sub-$5K first-responder-class drones and run one head-to-head on range, wind and latency, then publish it. Email 200 police tech sergeants and drone-as-first-responder coordinators and sign 10 agency subscriptions at $1,200. File public-records requests for existing agency test data to seed the second episode.

ideas.title: Flight Recorder for AI-Drafted Police Reports
ideas.angle: Pairing 2: Creator economy & media provenance x Government/public sector/defense/municipal services (process-based authorship proof x municipal policing)
ideas.one_liner: Vendor-agnostic middleware that captures the AI draft, every officer edit and timestamp, then issues a court-ready authorship record, the process-based 'human-made' proof creators lack, so prosecutors will accept AI-assisted reports.
ideas.customer: Police departments and sheriffs' offices ($60-150 per officer per year), city and county attorneys and DA offices that must vouch for reports, and public defender offices (per-case discovery audits).
ideas.problem: Tools such as Axon's Draft One write narratives from body-cam audio, and reporting in 2025 said original AI drafts are not retained (prior knowledge). California SB 524 (effective 2026) requires disclosure of AI use and retention of first drafts, Utah requires disclaimers, and King County prosecutors said in 2024 they would reject AI-assisted reports (prior knowledge). Defense has the same failure mode: a SOCOM analyst's chatbot fabricated a ship's cargo manifest that was formatted as an official intelligence summary, with no provenance layer in the workflow.
ideas.solution: A capture layer inside the report editor or records-management system logs the body-cam transcript hash, the AI draft, each officer edit as a diff, and time-on-task, with per-paragraph officer attestations ('I observed' or 'I reviewed'). It emits a signed content-credential-style record attached to the report, a redacted discovery packet for defense, and a DA-portal view that applies each office's acceptance rules.
ideas.why_now: State laws requiring disclosure and draft retention are in force in 2026. AI report-writing is spreading while DA acceptance remains the gate. Process-based provenance standards (C2PA) now exist, and GenAI.mil's 2M-user rollout shows the same official-looking-AI-text problem is arriving federally.
ideas.revenue_model: Per-officer SaaS, per-case discovery-packet fees to public defenders, and later federal licenses for labeling AI-assisted analytic products.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck to AI report-writing is admissibility and credibility, not accuracy, and the real gatekeepers are DAs, not police chiefs. A DA who publishes an acceptance standard requiring a verifiable authorship record forces every vendor to comply, so give the standard to DAs first and sell the ledger to departments second.
ideas.first_30_days: Get one DA's office in a state with an SB 524-style law to co-draft an acceptance standard. Prototype a Word and Google Docs add-in plus a records-system-neutral upload, pilot it with 2 small departments already testing AI report tools, and offer public defenders an 'AI-report discovery audit' service.

ideas.title: Signed Eyewitness Network for Ports and Sanctions
ideas.angle: Pairing 2: Creator economy & media provenance x Government/public sector/defense/municipal services (signed capture by hobbyist creators x defense/dual-use OSINT)
ideas.one_liner: A network of ship, plane and port spotters and local creators paid per provenance-signed capture (verified time, place and device), sold first to maritime insurers and sanctions teams and next to Coast Guard, Navy and intelligence analysts.
ideas.customer: Sanctions-compliance teams at banks, commodity traders and marine insurers or P&I brokers ($40-150 per verified task, $2-5K/month watchlist subscriptions). Later buyers are Coast Guard, CBP, NGA and defense OSINT analysts through SBIR or commercial solutions openings.
ideas.problem: Open-source analysis is bottlenecked on 'who shot this and when', not on analysis. AI fakes and unverified feeds enter analytic workflows: a SOCOM analyst's chatbot fabricated a cargo manifest and aircraft were airborne before the error was caught, while Maven now has 100K+ users and leaders admit gaps in logistics data visibility. Hobbyist spotters and drone and dashcam creators already sit at chokepoints, but their images cannot be trusted, priced or bought.
ideas.solution: Buyers post look-and-verify tasks ('is tanker X at berth Y today?'). Spotters reply with C2PA-signed captures from phones with native content credentials (prior knowledge: recent Pixel and Samsung models). The platform validates the signature chain, GNSS and time, and cross-checks sun angle, weather and AIS, then packages an analyst-ready evidence artifact with a spotter reputation score. Buyers purchase a signed artifact, not labor, so this is not a freelancer marketplace.
ideas.why_now: Native camera signing shipped on mainstream phones (prior knowledge) and C2PA reached spec 2.3, so no proprietary hardware is needed. Sanctions and shadow-fleet enforcement and the 2026 Iran conflict raise verification demand, and GenAI.mil put AI summarization in front of 2M users, making trusted ground-truth inputs the scarce resource.
ideas.revenue_model: Per-task fees with a 30% platform take, watchlist subscriptions, and government contracts later.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: AI is making analysis abundant and cheap while trusted ground truth stays scarce. The hobbyist spotter community is an existing, unpaid, reputation-rich sensor network, and because phones now sign captures a two-person team can build the verification layer instead of hardware.
ideas.first_30_days: Recruit 30 spotters from ship- and plane-spotting forums in two port cities. Take 10 paid pilot tasks at about $75 from a marine insurance broker or sanctions consultancy, build the verification pipeline around C2PA validation plus AIS cross-checks, and then apply to an SBIR or commercial solutions opening on commercial ground truth.

ideas.title: Compliance Co-op for Group-Buy Hobby Hardware
ideas.angle: Pairing 1: Legal services, compliance & new regulations (EU AI Act, privacy, PFAS, right to repair, etc.) x Weird, niche and overlooked markets (hobbies, collectibles, faith communities, subcultures)
ideas.one_liner: A pooled EU compliance desk (CRA incident reporting, EU responsible person, battery/e-waste registrations, SBOM monitoring) that lets one-person keyboard, FPV, synth and LoRa hardware makers keep selling to Europe.
ideas.customer: Boutique hardware makers of 1-20 people in enthusiast scenes: custom mechanical keyboards, eurorack/synth modules, FPV drone boards, LoRa/Meshtastic radios, 3D-printer upgrade kits. They sell through group buys, Tindie, Kickstarter and Discord shops, including US and Asian makers shipping into the EU/UK, plus the boutique vendors that resell them.
ideas.problem: Per the briefing, the EU Cyber Resilience Act's 24-hour vulnerability/incident reporting duty went live 11 Sep 2026 for products with digital elements, Data Act connected-product design duties began 12 Sep 2026, and full CRA conformity is due 11 Dec 2027 (fines up to EUR 15M or 2.5% of turnover). Those duties fall on whoever sells the product, and in hobby scenes that is a hobbyist selling a 300-unit run built on open-source firmware (QMK, Betaflight, Klipper, Meshtastic). The CRA's open-source carve-out protects non-commercial projects, not the person selling hardware with the firmware. Stack on the EU General Product Safety Regulation's EU-responsible-person requirement (in force since Dec 2024), radio-equipment cybersecurity rules, and battery and WEEE registrations (battery labelling duties start around Aug 2026, verify), and the makers' choices are to ignore it or stop shipping to the EU. A EUR 5-10k consultancy engagement is impossible on an $80-300 product.
ideas.solution: A membership 'compliance-of-record' co-op. Members get: a named EU responsible person and CRA contact of record (professional-indemnity insured); a shared coordinated-vulnerability-disclosure desk with a tested runbook for filing on ENISA's single reporting platform within 24 hours; a CI plug-in that generates SBOMs and watches firmware dependencies (QMK, ChibiOS, ESP-IDF, Zephyr etc.) for exploited CVEs; declaration-of-conformity and technical-file templates by product class; a battery/EPR registration bundle; and a group-buy contract addendum covering delivery windows and customised-goods withdrawal rights. The co-op also acts as liaison to upstream open-source firmware projects and channels 'sponsored security fixes' to them.
ideas.why_now: CRA reporting has been live for about 18 days and the Data Act design duties for 17 (per briefing). Market-surveillance sweeps and marketplace delistings typically follow such dates, and marketplaces already delist listings that lack GPSR data. Full conformity lands 11 Dec 2027, so scenes will look for a shared answer during 2026-27, before any vendor has locked the niche.
ideas.revenue_model: Annual dues tiered by EU units shipped (about EUR 390/yr up to 500 units, EUR 1,200 up to 5,000, custom above). Per-SKU onboarding fee of EUR 250-750. Optional micro-levy of EUR 0.10-0.25 per unit that funds the incident desk and upstream firmware maintainers. Paid 'CRA sprint' for makers with more than 5 SKUs.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Regulators wrote these rules for companies with a compliance department, but the enthusiast hardware economy is thousands of micro-manufacturers who share the same three failure points: firmware dependencies, 24-hour incident reporting, and an EU address. The scalable unit of compliance is the scene or firmware ecosystem, not the individual maker. A co-op that pools the boring 80% and is trusted inside the scene's Discords beats both a law firm and a generic authorised-representative vendor, because reputation in the scene is the distribution channel.
ideas.first_30_days: Pick one scene (custom keyboards on QMK/VIA, or LoRa/Meshtastic). Interview 15 makers from group-buy vendor lists. Have a compliance lawyer and a firmware engineer write a one-page '24-hour CRA reporting runbook' and post it free in the scene's Discords, r/MechanicalKeyboards and Geekhack. Sign 10 founding members at about EUR 250 for year one, deliver an incident-reporting drill and a template technical file for one product class, and sell fixed-price single-SKU audits. Cost is two part-time experts plus a simple site, and break-even is roughly 40 members.

ideas.title: Yes-in-God's-Backyard Deal Desk for Congregations
ideas.angle: Pairing 1: Legal services, compliance & new regulations (EU AI Act, privacy, PFAS, right to repair, etc.) x Weird, niche and overlooked markets (hobbies, collectibles, faith communities, subcultures)
ideas.one_liner: A fixed-fee service that tells a shrinking congregation and its denomination what its land can legally become (by-right housing, ground lease, sale, merger), then runs the governance, title and buyer process.
ideas.customer: Regional denominational bodies (presbyteries, dioceses, Methodist conferences, Lutheran synods, synagogue federations) and boards of congregations with 50-250 members that hold a large building and lot they cannot afford to maintain. Secondary payers are affordable-housing developers and community land trusts that need sites.
ideas.problem: Per the briefing, only 33% of Americans attend monthly, Christian share has plateaued near 62%, and 18-24-year-olds are only 46% Christian, so many congregations sit on oversized buildings whose upkeep drains endowments. Selling is legally tangled: denominational trust clauses and canon-law approval thresholds, donor-restricted funds and cemeteries, state attorney-general notice for charitable assets, historic designation, and zoning. Lay boards typically wait for a crisis and then accept the first offer, usually an investor or another church. Meanwhile housing-shortage politics have produced by-right housing on religious land laws (California SB 4 took effect in 2024, with similar bills in other states, verify list), so the land may be worth multiples of the building, but few boards know it.
ideas.solution: Lead with a $1,500-3,000 'Land Options Report' covering parcel and zoning analysis under the state's faith-land housing law, likely unit yield, estimated residual land value against as-is sale, a title and restriction checklist, and a governance map of who must approve (trust clause, canon law, AG notice). Then sell a fixed-fee 'Transition Package': sequenced legal steps, member-vote scripts and communications, an RFP to pre-qualified faith-friendly developers (ground lease with a worship-space carve-out, so the congregation keeps a chapel and gets rent), and closing management. The report is automated with county parcel data plus LLM extraction of zoning code, reviewed by a real-estate/nonprofit attorney.
ideas.why_now: Pew's 2025 finding that decline has leveled but the generational gap is steep (briefing) means closures will keep coming for years. By-right faith-land housing laws are new (California SB 4 effective 2024, more states 2025-26, verify) and few boards know they exist. Cheap parcel data and LLM zoning-code reading make a $1,500 report profitable, where it used to need a $15k consultant.
ideas.revenue_model: Report fee of $1.5-3k, paid by congregations or as a bulk judicatory contract of $25-60k per year. Transition package at a fixed $15-40k or 1.5-3% of transaction value. Developer-side site-sourcing retainer or finder's fee, structured around broker-licensing rules.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The scarce resource is not money or developers but a governance process a lay board can survive: each closure has 4-6 approval gates and any one can veto it. The value sits in a pre-mapped approval path for each denomination's polity. Under by-right housing, the residual land value often exceeds the building's as-is price, so the congregation that thinks it must close can instead become a landlord with a rent-paying chapel. Church brokers and developers each see only half of this.
ideas.first_30_days: Choose one state with a faith-land housing law and one denomination whose polity is well documented. Offer free Land Options Reports to 10 congregations referred by a regional official, in exchange for case-study rights and a $500 deposit. Hire a part-time real-estate/nonprofit attorney, assemble county GIS and zoning data, and pre-qualify 3 developers. Aim for 3-5 paid reports and one transition engagement within six months.

ideas.title: Permit Concierge for Rare-Plant and Reptile Sellers
ideas.angle: Pairing 1: Legal services, compliance & new regulations (EU AI Act, privacy, PFAS, right to repair, etc.) x Weird, niche and overlooked markets (hobbies, collectibles, faith communities, subcultures)
ideas.one_liner: A checkout-integrated paperwork and permit service that lets hobby breeders of orchids, aroids, cacti, tarantulas and reptiles legally fill foreign orders instead of pushing buyers to the gray market.
ideas.customer: Independent rare-plant sellers (Instagram, Etsy, Facebook groups), hobby reptile/amphibian/invertebrate breeders, and small orchid/succulent nurseries doing $3k+/month that keep turning away foreign orders. Expo organizers and hobby societies (aroid, orchid, reptile expos) are a channel.
ideas.problem: All orchids and cacti, plus many other hobby species, are CITES-listed. Cross-border shipments need phytosanitary certificates, CITES export/import permits (which vary by country and by whether specimens are artificially propagated), US Lacey Act declarations, and import-inspection compliance on the EU/UK side. CITES CoP20 (Nov-Dec 2025) added listings that phase in during 2026 (verify). The paperwork is per-shipment, per-country and slow, so honest sellers refuse foreign orders, buyers turn to smugglers, and a small mistake means seizure or fines.
ideas.solution: A per-shipment service. The seller enters species and origin (propagated or wild). The system determines required documents by destination (CITES appendix and exemptions, phytosanitary certificate, carrier acceptance rules), pre-fills forms, books inspections and generates paperwork packets. It maintains a 'propagation record book' for each seller (dated photos, invoices, mother-plant records) to evidence the artificially-propagated exemption. A Shopify/Etsy plug-in quotes or blocks foreign orders with the permit fee included. A licensed customs broker/permit expeditor is the operating partner, and a wildlife-law attorney handles edge cases.
ideas.why_now: New CITES listings from CoP20 phase in through 2026 (verify). Post-Brexit UK rules and the EU Plant Health Regulation (fully applicable since Dec 2019) mean plant parcels need phytosanitary certificates, and platform and law-enforcement attention to online wildlife trade keeps rising. Rare-plant and exotic-pet hobby demand stayed high after 2020, so more sellers are hitting the cliff.
ideas.revenue_model: $89-349 per shipment. $39/month pro plan that includes the propagation record book and checkout plug-in. Referral fees from carriers/brokers. Sponsored compliance desks at hobby expos.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Enforcement targets traffickers, but the practical legal cliff is for honest small sellers. The exemption for artificially propagated specimens means documentation of propagation is the real product: a provenance book. A seller with a clean book can charge a premium and reach EU/UK buyers competitors cannot, and a 'permit-verified' badge becomes a moat as platforms tighten.
ideas.first_30_days: Pick one lane, either CITES-listed succulents/orchids US-to-EU/UK or captive-bred reptiles. Partner with an experienced permit expeditor. Publish a free 'what paperwork does my plant need' checker to collect leads. Sign 10 sellers with pending foreign orders and process 30 shipments at about $150 each. Use the results to build templates and the propagation-book format.

ideas.title: Privacy-Compliant Monetization for Faith Apps
ideas.angle: Pairing 1: Legal services, compliance & new regulations (EU AI Act, privacy, PFAS, right to repair, etc.) x Weird, niche and overlooked markets (hobbies, collectibles, faith communities, subcultures)
ideas.one_liner: An audit-plus-replacement stack for small prayer, Quran, Bible, Torah and temple apps whose ad SDKs quietly turn every user into a sale of religious-belief data.
ideas.customer: Independent and mid-size publishers of ad-funded faith apps (prayer times, Quran, Bible/devotional, Hindu calendar, Zmanim, halal finders, congregation apps) and church-management/giving software vendors serving thousands of congregations.
ideas.problem: Religious beliefs are special-category data under GDPR Art. 9 and 'sensitive data' requiring opt-in consent under nearly every US state privacy law. Maryland's law goes further, banning the sale of sensitive data and limiting collection to what is strictly necessary (in force since Oct 2025, verify enforcement dates). Regulators have treated mere use of a niche app as revealing sensitive traits (Norway's Grindr fine, upheld on appeal, verify). Reporting in 2020 showed a Muslim prayer app's location data reaching a broker and then US military contractors. Yet most small faith apps run stock ad SDKs with device IDs and location, have no consent flow and no counsel. The briefing notes non-Christian faith apps are far less served than Hallow-style Christian ones, and the IAPP says state privacy momentum is at an all-time high.
ideas.solution: (1) A public audit tool that scans app binaries and web properties for SDK data flows and issues a scorecard plus a legal-risk memo by state and EU. (2) A drop-in compliance SDK: a consent manager that treats every user as sensitive by default, server-side region logic, data maps and DPIA templates in Arabic, Urdu, Bahasa, Hebrew, Spanish and Portuguese. (3) A contextual, ID-free sponsorship marketplace where halal, kosher, umrah, church-goods and faith-nonprofit sponsors book placements by content context (for example an iftar-times page). (4) A subpoena and data-request playbook with minimal retention by design, so the app has little to hand over.
ideas.why_now: State privacy laws with sensitive-data opt-in are now the norm and Maryland's strict rules are enforceable in 2026 (verify dates). GDPR fines total EUR 7.16B with 229 new cases in 2026 (per briefing). Faith apps are booming (Hallow reached #1 in the US App Store) while faith data is politically charged around surveillance and immigration enforcement.
ideas.revenue_model: $149-499/month per app for SDK plus audit. 25-30% revenue share on contextual sponsorship. One-time $1.5-3k audit and fix sprint. Enterprise contracts with church-tech vendors.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: For a faith app the category itself reveals the belief (the Grindr logic), so 'we do not collect religion' is not a defense. The violation is the ad model, so the fix is a different revenue stream, not a policy PDF. Contextual sponsorship from faith-community advertisers can pay better than junk programmatic. Public scorecards create the sales funnel, because in tight communities reputation and fear move fast.
ideas.first_30_days: Audit the top 100 Muslim prayer/Quran apps and 50 Christian, Jewish and Hindu apps with open-source traffic analysis (mitmproxy, Exodus-style trackers). Publish a 'Privacy Scorecard for Faith Apps' and email each publisher. Sell paid fix sprints to 5 pilot apps at about $2k and recruit 5 community sponsors for contextual placements. Team is one privacy lawyer plus one Android engineer.

ideas.title: Collective Anti-Piracy Desk for 3D-Print Miniature Creators
ideas.angle: Pairing 1: Legal services, compliance & new regulations (EU AI Act, privacy, PFAS, right to repair, etc.) x Weird, niche and overlooked markets (hobbies, collectibles, faith communities, subcultures)
ideas.one_liner: A creator-owned enforcement collective that fingerprints STL/3D-print models, hunts leaks across Telegram, Discord and marketplaces, and uses EU Digital Services Act notice, trusted-flagger and appeal rights to make takedowns stick.
ideas.customer: Independent sculptors and small studios selling printable miniatures, terrain and tabletop models via Patreon, Kickstarter, MyMiniFactory, Cults3D and their own stores (tens of thousands worldwide, top creators earning six figures). Also indie designers of other collectible models (keyboard cases, cosplay props) and the hosting platforms that want a clean enforcement feed.
ideas.problem: Files leak within days of release, spread through Discord and Telegram, get resold on Etsy/eBay/Temu-style marketplaces and printed into physical minis. A solo creator faces hundreds of infringements a month, and one-by-one DMCA notices cost hours, are ignored or are countered by repeat offenders. Brand-protection vendors price for brands, not solo sculptors. The EU Digital Services Act gave structured levers (Art. 16 notice-and-action, Art. 17 statements of reasons, Art. 21 out-of-court dispute bodies, Art. 22 trusted-flagger priority) and put very large marketplaces such as Temu and AliExpress under Commission supervision, but nobody has packaged these levers for small creators.
ideas.solution: (1) Geometry-based mesh fingerprinting, robust to re-meshing, scaling, splitting and hollowing, plus image similarity for renders and prints, with crawlers for leak channels, marketplaces and cloud-drive links. (2) A case engine that files DMCA and DSA notices in correct legal form, tracks counter-notices and statements of reasons, and escalates repeat infringers to the platform's regulator complaint channels. (3) An EU-established entity built to apply for DSA trusted-flagger status; Art. 22 explicitly favors bodies that represent collective interests and are independent of platforms. (4) A 'legit copy' program that offers print farms and Etsy resellers a licensed route, so leaks become royalty income.
ideas.why_now: The printable-model economy on Patreon and 3D-printer adoption are at scale. The DSA has been fully applicable since Feb 2024 and the Commission's 2025 actions against Temu/AliExpress make regulator escalation credible (verify status). AI re-meshing and generative 3D tools make exact-hash detection obsolete. Pressure from IP owners like Games Workshop pushes hobbyists toward original designs, so creator-owned IP is growing.
ideas.revenue_model: Subscriptions of $29-149/month by catalog size. 10-20% share of licensed royalties recovered from converted resellers. Enterprise feed for hosting platforms that want a vetted trusted-flagger channel.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Piracy at this scale is a coordination problem. Thirty thousand creators each losing $5-50k cannot afford lawyers, but as a collective with formal DSA status they generate volume and quality that platforms must prioritise. The realistic prize is converting pirates into licensees (print farms reselling legally), not just takedown counts.
ideas.first_30_days: Sign 10 mid-tier Patreon sculptors for a free 30-day leak report. Build the fingerprint and crawler MVP with open-source mesh-hashing plus CLIP embeddings. Send DMCA/DSA notices through a part-time attorney and measure takedown rates. Convert reports to $49/month subscriptions. Register the EU entity and start the trusted-flagger application with counsel.

ideas.title: Market Surveillance for Entertainment Prediction Markets
ideas.angle: Pairing 2: Gaming, entertainment, live experiences, fandoms x Cybersecurity, deepfake fraud, identity verification, scams targeting consumers and businesses
ideas.one_liner: Sportradar-style integrity monitoring for the boom in prediction-market contracts on awards, charts, box office and game releases, where insiders and bot farms can swing outcomes.
ideas.customer: CFTC-regulated prediction-market exchanges and brokers that list entertainment contracts (Kalshi-type venues and the betting and brokerage firms entering the space). Secondary buyers are rights holders and award bodies (studios, labels, game publishers, guilds) that want to know when their confidential information is being traded.
ideas.problem: Per the briefing, Kalshi went from about $11B to $22B valuation in 2026, entertainment and awards are already about 11% of its activity, and states are fighting the venues. Exchanges must list contracts that are not readily susceptible to manipulation and run surveillance, but their tooling is built for sports and finance. Entertainment outcomes can be moved by insiders (PR staff, awards accountants, streaming-platform employees, contractors who know game release dates), by bot-farmed streams and votes, by review-bombing, and by leaked builds and schedules. Resolution sources (Spotify charts, Rotten Tomatoes, Steam counts, box office) are each gameable in a different way.
ideas.solution: (1) A 'contract risk review' done before an entertainment market lists: score the resolution source for manipulability (cost to swing it, for example streams or votes needed) and the insider population (who knows the outcome and how many people), then recommend rules such as delayed settlement, position limits and source hierarchies. (2) Live surveillance that flags anomalous trading, such as fresh accounts trading ahead of announcements or positions timed with leak or stream-spike signals, cross-referenced with external manipulation indicators (streaming bot networks, vote farms). (3) Investigation and referral packages for exchanges and regulators. (4) A rights-holder subscription that alerts when a contract references their confidential events.
ideas.why_now: Kalshi's valuation doubled in five months and new entrants are listing culture contracts. Multiple states are attacking event contracts, so demonstrable surveillance is now a legal-defense asset. GTA VI launches 19 Nov 2026 and Q4 award season and Spotify Wrapped create dense culture-contract activity. AI-cheap bot streaming and vote farms lower manipulation costs, and Chainalysis notes scam tooling now sells for about $50 (per briefing).
ideas.revenue_model: Annual retainer of $60-250k per exchange for the surveillance feed. $2-10k per contract risk review. Rights-holder alert subscriptions of $2-5k/month. Hourly investigation and expert-witness work.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Sports-integrity firms never learned how an awards accountant or a streaming intern leaks, and entertainment insiders are far more numerous and less regulated than athletes. Resolution sources are commercial dashboards, not referees. The buyer's budget is really a legal-defense budget for defending the product state by state.
ideas.first_30_days: One fraud/market-abuse analyst plus one music/film/game data specialist. Publish a 'manipulation cost' analysis of the 10 most-traded entertainment contracts (Oscar categories, Spotify top artist, Steam concurrent players, Rotten Tomatoes scores) and send it to compliance heads at 5 exchanges. Offer a 30-day paid pilot review of upcoming contracts (GTA VI launch, award season) at $10-15k.

ideas.title: Payee-Verification Network for the Live Music Business
ideas.angle: Pairing 2: Gaming, entertainment, live experiences, fandoms x Cybersecurity, deepfake fraud, identity verification, scams targeting consumers and businesses
ideas.one_liner: A shared, industry-vouched directory of who is really entitled to be paid in the touring economy (agencies, promoters, venues, production vendors), checked before every deposit wire.
ideas.customer: Independent and mid-size booking agencies, regional promoters, festivals, tour accountants and business managers, and production, trucking and staging vendors. Starting wedge is 50-200 person agencies and promoters that wire 50% artist deposits.
ideas.problem: Live touring runs on large advance wires: artist-guarantee deposits, production advances and vendor prepayments, with banking details passed through PDF contracts and email across dozens of small counterparties whose bookers, agents and accountants change often. That is ideal business-email-compromise territory (US BEC losses $3.05B in 2025 per FBI IC3), and now voice clones make 'the agent called to change the account' credible (a vendor report claims 680% year-over-year growth in voice-deepfake attacks). The FBI fund-freeze process recovered 58% of attempted funds but only when victims act fast, and each bank sees only its own side. Europe's mandatory Verification of Payee on euro transfers (from Oct 2025) checks name against IBAN only inside the euro zone, and the US has nothing similar, while tours mix currencies and countries.
ideas.solution: Verify each entity once (KYB, identity of authorised signers, bank account proven by micro-deposit or open banking) and publish signed payment instructions. Settlement spreadsheets and accounting tools check payees against the network before a wire is released, via a plug-in for spreadsheets, Slack and common accounting software. Any change of banking details triggers out-of-band, multi-party confirmation (agent, manager and accountant, never a reply-to email), with a 24-72 hour cooling-off for first payments. A bank hot-line handshake speeds recall and freeze on suspected misdirection. Each deal also generates a shared verbal code phrase to defeat cloned-voice calls.
ideas.why_now: IC3's 2025 numbers, AI-enabled scam operations earning about 4.5x more than others (Chainalysis, per briefing), and cheap voice cloning. Live Nation's $25.2B revenue and its arena buying show the sector's money is growing and consolidating, so more wires move through more small counterparties. EU Verification of Payee shows regulators' direction but leaves the cross-border and hybrid gap open.
ideas.revenue_model: SaaS of $99-499/month per verified entity. Per-payment verification fee of $2-5 or 0.02-0.05% for high-value wires. Bank and payments-provider licensing. Insurance partnerships where crime/cyber insurers discount premiums for network members.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Payments-fraud vendors sell to banks and large corporates, but the live industry is thousands of small counterparties whose trust is relationship-based. The relationship graph (who is the legitimate agent, manager or accountant for whom) lives in people's heads, so the moat is a graph the industry vouches for itself. Once most deposits flow through the network, an unverified change-of-details request becomes an obvious red flag.
ideas.first_30_days: Partner with 2-3 mid-size booking agencies or tour accountants (the people whose wires get hit). Give them a free payment-instruction registry as a spreadsheet plus Slack or Chrome extension. Capture verified bank details for their top 100 counterparties. Run a consented voice-clone fire drill to create urgency. Charge $199/month per agency by day 60 and approach two insurers for premium-discount pilots.

ideas.title: Leak-Proof Outsourcing Passport for Game Studios
ideas.angle: Pairing 2: Gaming, entertainment, live experiences, fandoms x Cybersecurity, deepfake fraud, identity verification, scams targeting consumers and businesses
ideas.one_liner: Contractor identity checks at first build access, per-recipient build watermarking and reusable vendor security attestations for the outsourcing chain (art, audio, QA, porting) that leaks unreleased games.
ideas.customer: Mid-size and AA/indie publishers that outsource to 20-200 external vendors. Also the vendors themselves (art studios in Poland, Vietnam, India and elsewhere, QA houses, localization and voice studios, freelance marketplaces) who need a portable credential to win work.
ideas.problem: Layoffs and cost-cutting push more production to external vendors and freelancers. Per the briefing, Ubisoft headcount fell from 18,666 to 16,590 and EA's $55B buyout, which closed 4 Aug 2026, aims to cut operating costs by putting AI throughout. Each vendor has weaker security than the publisher while unreleased builds are the crown jewels (GTA VI launches 19 Nov 2026, and past leaks like Rockstar 2022, Insomniac 2023 and Game Freak 2024 show the pattern). Remote contractors are also prime targets for identity fraud: North Korean IT-worker schemes hit 'nearly 70' and 'over 100' US companies in cases sentenced in Apr-May 2026, using deepfake-assisted interviews and stolen identities. Film has the MPA's Trusted Partner Network; games have no equivalent.
ideas.solution: A subscription 'passport' with five parts. (1) Contractor identity verification with liveness and injection-attack detection at onboarding and again at first privileged build access, tied to device posture. (2) A game-specific vendor security attestation, evidence-based (SSO, endpoint, repo hygiene) and shared across publishers so a vendor is assessed once. (3) Per-recipient forensic watermarking of builds, assets and design documents so a leak can be traced to a person or vendor. (4) Offboarding automation for contract end or layoff waves. (5) Insurer-ready evidence packages for cyber and E&O cover.
ideas.why_now: EA's leveraged buyout, Ubisoft's restructuring and Tencent-backed Vantage carve-out are all driving outsourcing. GTA VI's launch date will attract extortion attempts. North Korean IT-worker cases and deepfake interview kits make hiring-time identity checks insufficient. The IDScan.net breach (153M license scans) makes zero-retention verification a selling point (per briefing), and enterprise identity products are crowded but none focus on game supply chains.
ideas.revenue_model: Publishers pay $1.5-6k/month plus $30-80 per contractor-month. Vendors pay $200-500/month for a portable attestation badge, giving vendor-pays adoption. Watermarking priced per build distribution.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: The bottleneck is not the publisher's own security but that each publisher re-audits the same few hundred vendors. A shared 'assess once, reuse everywhere' passport (film's TPN model) is cheaper for publishers and turns vendors into paying customers. Identity must be verified at the moment of privileged access rather than at hiring, because proxy interviews and deepfakes defeat interview-time checks.
ideas.first_30_days: Partner with 2-3 mid-size publishers or a co-dev/QA outsourcer. Draft a 40-question game-specific assessment, wire up an existing IDV API plus a device-posture check, and pilot with one outsourcing vendor. Offer a 'leak-trace drill' using watermarks on a demo build. Sell to publishers' security leads at $1.5k/month pilots.

ideas.title: Ticket Escrow Bot for Fan Communities
ideas.angle: Pairing 2: Gaming, entertainment, live experiences, fandoms x Cybersecurity, deepfake fraud, identity verification, scams targeting consumers and businesses
ideas.one_liner: A payment-escrow bot for the Discord, WhatsApp and Facebook groups where fans already swap tickets, releasing money only when a cryptographically verifiable ticket-transfer email arrives.
ideas.customer: Fans aged 18-35 (K-pop, pop tours, esports, festivals, football supporters) trading tickets peer-to-peer, and the community admins and moderators who police scams manually. Fans pay the fee, and admins get a revenue share.
ideas.problem: Ticket fraud thrives in fan groups because the only 'proof' is a screenshot, and generative AI now forges tickets, receipts and transfer confirmations trivially. Official resale is distrusted: per the briefing, Oasis tickets went from GBP 135 to 350+ under dynamic pricing, StubHub's World Cup 2026 tickets failed to reach buyers with class actions following, and the UK CMA ordered StubHub to refund 50,000+ customers over drip pricing. Fans therefore keep swapping in groups, where scammers pretend to transfer tickets or sell the same ticket several times.
ideas.solution: The buyer pays into escrow. The seller performs the official transfer in the ticketing app (Ticketmaster, AXS, Eventim, Fever and similar). The buyer sends the platform's 'tickets received' email to a unique escrow address, either forwarded as an .eml attachment or through a narrowly scoped read-only mailbox filter for that sender only. The system validates the DKIM/ARC signature, sender domain, event, section and seat lines, and that the recipient is the buyer, then releases funds after a hold for barcode rotation. Extras: automatic enforcement of a group's face-value cap, light seller verification above thresholds, an admin-facing reputation ledger, and cancellation refunds through an insurance partner. Payments run through a licensed platform-payments partner rather than holding funds directly.
ideas.why_now: AI-forged screenshots have made image evidence worthless. Per the briefing, Live Nation lost a federal jury verdict on monopolization in April 2026 and resale fees are under fire, the FTC's all-in pricing rule took effect in May 2025, and StubHub's delivery failures have left fans without a trusted route. Ticketing platforms increasingly move tickets by wallet transfer, so signed transfer emails are now standard.
ideas.revenue_model: 4-6% fee on escrowed amount, split between buyer and seller, with 0.5-1% shared with community admins. Premium 'insured swap' add-on. B2B API for promoters that want a safe official fan-swap channel.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: You do not need to beat Ticketmaster or become a marketplace. Every major ticketing platform already emits a DKIM-signed transfer email that is very hard to fake, a cheap trust anchor no fan-group scammer can produce. The distribution channel is community admins, who already do unpaid trust-and-safety work and will adopt anything that reduces their scam reports.
ideas.first_30_days: Pick one fandom with a high-volume swap group (a K-pop tour or a football supporters' group). Run concierge escrow by hand with a payments-platform account and a script that checks .eml DKIM. Handle 100 swaps at 5% and publish 'scams avoided' stats. Onboard 10 admin partners with a revenue share. Check ticketing terms of service per market before scaling.

ideas.title: Live-Action Fraud Drills Using Immersive Theater
ideas.angle: Pairing 2: Gaming, entertainment, live experiences, fandoms x Cybersecurity, deepfake fraud, identity verification, scams targeting consumers and businesses
ideas.one_liner: Ticketed and B2B immersive-theater experiences where participants, with consent, get scammed by actors and voice-cloned 'relatives' in a safe space and learn the tells under real emotional pressure.
ideas.customer: Credit unions, community banks and insurers that want measurable fraud-loss reduction among older customers; employers' security teams and finance, HR and IT-helpdesk staff (named targets of voice deepfakes); senior-living operators, libraries and AARP-style chapters. Escape-room and immersive-theater operators are licensees.
ideas.problem: Per the briefing, adults 60+ lost $7.7B in 2025 (up 59%), account for 66% of crypto-ATM losses, and law-enforcement-impersonation scams produced about 61,000 complaints and $1.6B+ with fake video calls. Conventional awareness training (videos, phishing simulations) shows little measurable effect; a 2025 study of about 19,500 UCSD Health employees found annual training had almost no impact on click rates (verify). Voice cloning now needs only 3 seconds of audio. The pressure tactics (urgency, secrecy, authority) are exactly what a lecture cannot simulate.
ideas.solution: A repeatable, franchisable 60-90 minute experience. Participants get a 'phone call' from an actor-controlled voice clone of a consenting volunteer (real-time voice conversion trained on the volunteer's own sample) or a fake CFO. They move through an escalating fraud script (fake bank, 'police', crypto-ATM instructions) with hidden facilitators, then a debrief teaches three tells and sets up a family or team safe-word protocol. Each participant leaves with a personalised safe-word card and help turning on their bank's trusted-contact feature. A B2B mobile 30-minute 'CFO voice-clone drill' scores the sponsor on how many people stop the transfer at each step. Outcomes are measured pre/post and at 90 days. Psychological-safety protocol and a counselor are built in.
ideas.why_now: October is Cybersecurity Awareness Month, when awareness budgets are spent. The FBI's 17 Sep 2026 PSA cites AI video calls in law-enforcement impersonation. Real-time voice conversion is cheap and voice-deepfake attacks are surging. Regulators are pushing banks to protect vulnerable customers (for example the UK's mandatory APP-fraud reimbursement since Oct 2024), so banks want provable prevention.
ideas.revenue_model: Sponsors pay $3-8k per community event of 30-60 participants, or $40-150 per employee for corporate drills. Licensing or franchise fees from venues (about $1.5k/month plus event share). Public ticketed shows at $25-40 with sponsor underwriting.
ideas.non_obvious_insight: Fraud victims are not ignorant. They are overwhelmed by staged emotion under time pressure, and skills learned in calm classrooms fail under stress. Live-experience designers know how to induce and safely release exactly that state, and security teams know the real scripts. Banks can also compute ROI in avoided losses, which theater companies cannot.
ideas.first_30_days: Pair an immersive-theater company with a fraud investigator. Prototype a 45-minute 'grandparent scam' and a 'CFO deepfake' scenario with consent forms and a licensed counselor. Pilot with two credit unions and one library during October at about $2.5k each. Measure pre/post behavior with a follow-up test call. Use results to sell to regional credit-union leagues and security-awareness teams.
